articles.title: House OKs on final reading stronger worker protection vs climate threats
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved on final reading a bill strengthening workers’ safety against climate-related threats and hazards. With 256 lawmakers voting…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved on final reading a bill strengthening workers’ safety against climate-related threats and hazards.

With 256 lawmakers voting in favor, the House Bill No. 10559, which reinforces Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) standards by integrating climate-adaptive measures was passed on third and final reading.
The bill also imposes stiffer penalties for OSH “gross violations thereof” that endanger workers.

The House Committee on Labor and Employment has earlier sponsored the measure amid unpredictable weather events that may threaten the safety and well-being of workers, primarily those working in outdoor settings.

“For construction workers exposed to intense heat and employees who must report for work amid heavy rains and severe weather, climate change is no longer an abstract issue but a danger they confront in earning their livelihood,” House Committee on Labor and Employment Chairperson Ramon Jolo Revilla said. /mr

articles.title: P7.78B needed to repair 2,243 schools damaged by monsoon, cyclones
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — At least 2,243 schools nationwide have reported damage from the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, with the Department of Education (DepEd)…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — At least 2,243 schools nationwide have reported damage from the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones, with the Department of Education (DepEd) estimating P7.78 billion would be needed for clearing, repairs and reconstruction.
In its situation report as of 8 a.m. Wednesday, Sept. 2, DepEd said rapid damage assessments based on requests from schools showed that 11,167 classrooms had been affected.
Of these, 6,530 classrooms sustained minor damage, 2,389 were classified as having major damage, while 2,248 were totally damaged.
Region III recorded the highest number of damage reports at 4,099, followed by Region I with 3,698 and the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) with 1,277.

Other reports came from Region IV-A with 938, Region VIII with 473, the National Capital Region with 299, Region IV-B with 212, Region II with 97, the Negros Island Region with 37, Region VI or Western Visayas with 19, and Region V with 18.
DepEd estimated that P65.036 million would be needed for clean-up and clearing operations covering 2,243 schools.
Another P319.970 million would be required for minor repairs in 1,487 schools, while P1.194 billion would be needed for major repairs in 669 schools.
The biggest requirement is for the reconstruction of facilities in 490 schools, estimated to cost P5.620 billion.
The damage was attributed to the combined effects of the southwest monsoon, or habagat, enhanced by tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, Neneng, Obet and Pilandok.
Meanwhile, 442 schools were being used as evacuation centers, accommodating 13,723 families in 1,748 classrooms.

CAR accounted for the largest number of schools serving as evacuation centers at 252, followed by the National Capital Region with 66, Region I with 58, Region III with 40, Region IV-A with 11, Region IV-B with eight and Region VIII with seven.
DepEd also reported that in-person classes were suspended Wednesday in 67 schools: 48 in Region III, 16 in CAR and three in Region I.

DepEd’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service said it was coordinating with field offices to monitor emerging impacts, validate class suspensions and facilitate the clearing and repair of affected schools.

School disaster risk reduction and management teams were also advised to remain operationally ready as prevailing weather conditions could still trigger localized flooding, landslides and other disruptions. INQ /mr

articles.title: Former Leyte Rep. Carmen Cari dies at 90
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — Former Leyte congresswoman and Baybay City mayor Carmen Cari, who played a key role in the cityhood of Baybay and the transformation of a state university into one of the country’s…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Former Leyte congresswoman and Baybay City mayor Carmen Cari, who played a key role in the cityhood of Baybay and the transformation of a state university into one of the country’s leading agriculture-focused institutions, died on Tuesday, Sept. 1, after a lingering illness. She was 90.

Cari spent nine years in Congress beginning in 2001, representing Leyte’s fifth congressional district. She later served as mayor of Baybay, where she helped push for the town’s conversion into a city in 2007.

At the time of her death, Cari was serving as a city councilor and president of the Philippine Councilors League-Leyte chapter. The latter position made her an ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
Her death was announced by her grandson, Carl Nicolas Cari. His father, Jose Cari, is the incumbent mayor of Baybay City.
“In every role she held and each endeavor she undertook, her abiding love for Leyteños never faltered,” Carl said in a statement released hours after his grandmother’s death.

“We honor the vibrant life of Mommy Carmen, which was marked by her unwavering dedication to public service, her grace under pressure, and her strength rooted in kindness. She has touched countless lives, and her legacy in the Kinto Distrito will live on forever,” he added.
The Baybay City government also mourned Cari, describing her as the “Mother of Baybay City.”

“Her passing is a great loss to Baybay City and to the many lives she touched through her years of public service,” the city government said in a statement. It extended its condolences to the Cari family, relatives, friends and others mourning her death.

Beyond her role in Baybay’s cityhood, Cari was also instrumental in the conversion of Leyte State University into Visayas State University. The institution has since become one of the country’s prominent universities specializing in agriculture and related fields.

Cari belonged to one of Leyte’s politically influential families. Among her relatives is incumbent Leyte Gov. Carlos Jericho Petilla, who served as secretary of energy during the administration of former President Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III.
Cari’s long career in public service spanned local and national government, with much of her political legacy tied to Baybay and Leyte’s fifth congressional district. INQ /mr

Three junior high school students from Philippine Science High School-Caraga create Ligtas Skwela, an innovative online platform for tracking student safety during emergencies, winning top honors at a regional tech competition

items: Three junior high school students from the Philippine Science High School-Caraga created an online platform called Ligtas Skwela to help schools track students during emergencies like fires and earthquakes.
The platform features two interfaces: Teacher Mode for reporting classroom conditions and Commander Mode for administrators to monitor classroom statuses and student whereabouts.
Ligtas Skwela won first place in a technology competition and the team plans to offer it through a subscription model, while also preparing to apply for a patent.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Three junior high school students from the Philippine Science High School-Caraga have developed an online platform designed to help schools track students during fires, earthquakes, and other emergencies within the school.
Called Ligtas Skwela, the platform is accessible online, allowing teachers and school administrators an overview of classrooms and students during an emergency.

The project won first place in the student category of the Startup Technology Pitching Competition during the Department of Science and Technology’s Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week in Caraga, held from August 27 to 29.
The team consists of project leader Kush Shekar, software developer Lorenzo Pariñas, and market research head Vic Andrei Hernando.
Pariñas said recent school emergencies, including the shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University, prompted the students to think about how schools account for students during a crisis.
“We’ve noticed that sometimes, in the system, they tend to not focus on the students and where they are in school,” Pariñas said.
Ligtas Skwela has two interfaces: Teacher Mode and Commander Mode.

Teachers can use the platform to report the condition of their classes, while Commander Mode provides administrators with information on classrooms, teachers, and their status, including whether a room is secure or whether people need medical assistance.
Instead of relying only on head counts, the system tracks students by name, allowing administrators to determine who is missing, Shekar said.

The developers said the website is functional but has so far only been tested on their campus. The current version requires an internet connection, although the team plans to develop an offline version.
They also plan to incorporate physical hardware, including buttons that could be used to conduct drills and trigger alarms.

The students envision offering Ligtas Skwela through a subscription model. Based on their current projections, it would cost P30,000 annually for a school with 1,000 students, or about P30 per student.
The team, mentored by engineer Lyndon Bermoy, was the only high school group among the nine finalists in the competition.
The students are also preparing to apply for a patent for the platform. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Police exhume body of former Czechoslovak foreign minister Jan Masaryk
articles.summary: The top diplomat was found dead on March 10, 1948, in the courtyard beneath his bathroom window, supposedly after a fall. Police said their probe aims to settle questions that have surrounded the…

image.caption: Some historians believe Jan Masaryk, seen as a pro-Western figure, may have been killed by Soviet agentsImage: AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Czech police said Wednesday they had begun exhuming the remains of former Czechoslovak Foreign Minister Jan Masaryk in an attempt to clear up speculation surrounding his death nearly 80 years ago.
In a statement posted to X, police said they planned to examine the remains, buried at Prague's Olsany Cemetery, "using the most modern forensic methods."
"We believe that today's actions will bring us closer to clarifying the circumstances leading to the death of Jan Masaryk," the statement said.
What happened to the former top diplomat?
Masaryk was found dead on March 10, 1948, dressed only in his pajamas, in the courtyard at the Foreign Ministry beneath his bathroom window.
The mysterious circumstances surrounding his death, at the height of the Cold War, have fueled speculation for decades.
At the time, the Interior Ministry claimed that he had committed suicide. Others believed his fall may have been an accident, or that he was murdered by Soviet agents.

blocks.caption: Jan Masaryk was found in the courtyard of the Foreign Ministy, housed in Prague's Czernin PalaceImage: UPI/dpa/picture-alliance

blocks.text: Who was Jan Masaryk?
Born in Prague on September 14, 1886, Masaryk was the son of the first Czechoslovak president, Tomas Garrigue Masaryk.
He served as the country's top diplomat from 1940 to 1948, first for the government-in-exile during World War II and then for the post-war coalition government.
Following the Czechoslovak communist coup of February 1948, he stayed on as foreign minister, refusing to step down.
The case of his death has been reviewed several times since the collapse of communism in the 1989 Velvet Revolution. The country later split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

blocks.caption: Jan Masaryk served as foreign minister during World War II and in the post-war government [File photo: 12 July, 1947]Image: Josef Mucha/CTK/picture alliance

articles.title: Blackout risk rises as heatwave stresses largest US electric grids
articles.summary:
US energy department warns of potential for outages in PJM Interconnection, serving 67 million from DC to Chicago

The risk ⁠of power outages ⁠is expected to ​escalate across a broad swath of…

blocks.text: The risk ⁠of power outages ⁠is expected to ​escalate across a broad swath of the United States on Wednesday as intense heat will test the capacity of electricity supplies ⁠serving millions of homes and businesses from the midwest through the mid-Atlantic.

The US Department of Energy warned of the potential for heightened blackout risks in ⁠the PJM Interconnection, the largest US electric grid, which serves 67 million people in ​a territory stretching from Washington DC to ‌Chicago.

Late on Tuesday night, ‌Chris Wright, the energy secretary, authorized PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a ‌last resort before declaring a level three energy emergency alert, which can be one of the last steps before rotating blackouts are ordered.
The energy department said the move was part of a plan “to stabilize the Mid-Atlantic grid and mitigate the risk of blackouts”.
“Maintaining affordable, reliable, and secure power for hardworking American families and businesses during ‌periods of hot weather is non-negotiable,” Wright said in a statement.
Temperatures in Chicago, St Louis and Washington DC were expected to rise above 90F (32C) during peak electricity demand.
PJM’s “maximum generation emergency” alert in effect early on Wednesday directed generators on planned outages to report how quickly they could return units to service.

Meanwhile, the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (Miso), the regional grid operator for 15 US states ⁠in the midwest and the south, predicted peak demand on Wednesday would approach ​record territory at ​about 121 gigawatts. Miso’s all-time high ​is 127.1 GW.
Miso warned of tight conditions and increased its normal reserve ​requirement as a ‌buffer against unexpected ​power plant outages and ​transmission line congestion.

In the Ozark region of rural Missouri, the Howell-Oregon Electric Cooperative advised customers to unplug unused chargers and appliances due to the continued extreme heat. Customers also were asked to consider raising their thermostats to reduce air conditioning use.

articles.title: No confidential funds in proposed 2027 OVP budget, says House Appro vice chair
articles.summary: There are no confidential funds in the proposed 2027 budget of the Office of the Vice President, House Committee on Appropriations Vice Chairperson Representative Jose Alvarez said.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 8:10pm
There are no confidential funds in the proposed 2027 budget of the Office of the Vice President, House Committee on Appropriations Vice Chairperson Representative Jose Alvarez said Wednesday.

"Wala. Nothing, nothing. So it is up to the president kung bigyan niya ng [if he will give] confidential funds yung Office of the Vice President. That is his discretion," Alvarez said in an ambush interview after the committee deliberations this afternoon, at which the OVP asked for P785 million for next year.
Alvarez also said there was no request from the OVP for confidential funds.
The impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte is currently tackling her use of the confidential funds allocated to the OVP and to the Department of Education when she was education secretary.
The Commission on Audit has issued notices of disallowance for the OVP confidential funds in 2022 and 2023.
Since then, the OVP has not been given any confidential fund.
Objection to parliamentary courtesy

During the deliberations of the House Committee on Appropriations on the proposed budget of the OVP today, BH Party-list Representative Robert Nazal moved to extend parliamentary courtesy to the OVP—the act of approving budget proposals without discussion, usually accorded to the President and the Vice President.

"Yesterday, this committee extended to the Office of the President a long-standing courtesy, passing its budget without interpellation in recognition of its standing as co-equal branch of government. Today, I respectfully ask the same courtesy to the Office of the Vice President," Nazal said.

"The vice president is currently facing the weight of an impeachment proceeding, a burden already heavy enough on its own. Her budget, moreover, has not grown. It remains modest and unremarkable," he added.
Several members of the committee objected to the motion, including House Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Party-list Representative Antonio Tinio.

"Nilinaw natin kahapon sa ating paliwanag na dapat ibasura na itong inter-parliamentary courtesy, lalo na pag usapin ng budget dahil nga tungkulin natin, ng lahat ng nasa gobyerno, ay maging transparent kung paano ginagamit ang pondo ng taumbayan," Tinio explained.

(We clarified yesterday about how we should junk this inter-parliamentary courtesy, especially when budgets are discussed, because it is the duty of all of us in this government to be transparent about how we use public funds.)

"Anong susunod dito? Another co-equal branch is the judiciary. Magmo-move na rin ba kayo na hindi na rin natin bubulatlatin o bubusisiin ang budget ng judiciary? Hindi naman yon nangyayari ever," he added.
(What next? Another co-equal branch is the judiciary. Are you also going to move that we do not discuss or scrutinize the judiciary's budget? That's not going to happen ever.)
He also called for an end to the said tradition.
"Kailangang itigil na po natin ang practice na ito. Anyway, I am sure handa naman na sagutin ng Office of the Vice President anumang tanong kaugnay sa kanilang budget ngayon," Tinio stated.
(We need to stop this practive. Anyway, I am sure the Office of the Vice President is ready to answer any questions we have regarding the proposed budget.)
Upon query of Alvarez, Nazal agreed to set aside his motion.
This was after OVP Chief of Staff Zuleika Lopez agreed to answer questions.
Alvarez said the OVP had written the committee two days ago to inform them that Lopez was representing the office in the budget deliberations.
Alvarez explained that it is usually the head of agency who defends the its budget proposal, but that an official with the rank of undersecretary is allowed to represent the agency.
Duterte has not attended the impeachment trial, at which staffers under her have already testified. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: EXPLAINER: How does haze affect your health?
articles.summary: Wildfires in Indonesia have burned about 200,000 hectares of land, producing thick haze that has spread to neighboring countries, including the Philippines.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 8:07pm
Wildfires in Indonesia have burned about 200,000 hectares of land, producing thick haze that has spread to neighboring countries, including the Philippines.
Indonesia has been working to contain the fires, but the prevailing El Niño phenomenon has made firefighting efforts more difficult. Smoke has blanketed several parts of the country.
According to a GMA News Feed report, the haze was observed in several parts of Metro Manila, CALABARZON and MIMAROPA.

In the National Capital Region, the air quality was classified as “very unhealthy” and “accurately unhealthy,” according to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources–Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB).
What is haze?

Haze is an atmospheric phenomenon in which fine particulate matter accumulates in the air. This includes PM2.5, or particles measuring 2.5 micrometers or smaller in diameter—about 30 times smaller than the width of a human hair.
How is air quality measured?
Experts measure the concentration of PM2.5 in the air and use it to determine the air quality category under the Air Quality Index.
The index has six categories: green for good, yellow for moderate, orange for unhealthy for sensitive groups, red for unhealthy, purple for very unhealthy, and maroon for hazardous.
How does PM2.5 affect the body?

Unlike larger particles such as dust, PM2.5 is small enough to bypass some of the body's natural defenses and penetrate deep into the respiratory system. These particles can reach the air sacs in the lungs and cause inflammation.

When air quality reaches the purple or “very unhealthy” level, exposure can pose health risks, particularly to sensitive groups. Fine particles can cause coughing, throat irritation, wheezing and difficulty breathing.
Exposure to high levels of PM2.5 can also worsen asthma and other existing lung conditions.

The particles can also enter the bloodstream and affect other parts of the body. Prolonged or high-level exposure to PM2.5 has been linked to cardiovascular problems, including an increased risk of heart attack and stroke.
Who is most vulnerable to haze?

The DENR-EMB reminded the public to limit outdoor activities in affected areas, especially people who are more sensitive to air pollution, including children, older adults, and those with lung or heart conditions.
For those who need to go outdoors, wearing a properly fitted N95 or equivalent respirator can help reduce exposure to fine particles.
The public is also advised to stay informed about air quality conditions and follow guidance from reliable government sources.— Jean Mangaluz with research from GMA DigiLab/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Solon: No secret funds in proposed budget for Office of Vice President
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — There are no confidential funds included in the proposed budget of the Office of Vice President (OVP) for 2027, according to Palawan Rep. Jose Alvarez on Wednesday. This was the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — There are no confidential funds included in the proposed budget of the Office of Vice President (OVP) for 2027, according to Palawan Rep. Jose Alvarez on Wednesday.
This was the answer of Alvarez, who serves as the vice chairperson of the House committee on appropriations, when asked if there are confidential funds proposed for the OVP in its budget next year.
“None. Nothing. So it’s up to the president it he wants to give OVP confidential funds. That’s his discretion,” Alvarez said in an ambush interview after the agency’s budget briefing.
The lawmaker also said that the OVP did not request for any secret funds in its 2027 budget.
During its budget briefing, the OVP presented its proposed budget worth P785.204 million under the 2027 National Expenditure Program.
This amount is significantly lower than the budget allocated in the 2026 General Appropriations Act worth P889.236 million.

A huge chunk of the proposed budget will be allocated for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses worth P561.651 million, followed by Personnel Services (P235.776 million); and Capital Outlay (P3.321 million).
Duterte was impeached by the House of Representatives last May 11 over the following four grounds:

Alleged misuse of confidential funds under the OVP and Department of Education (DepEd); alleged unexplained wealth; alleged distribution of monetary gifts or payments to DepEd officials; alleged assassination threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Marcos and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
As Duterte is facing trial before the impeachment court, the prosecution panel has started presenting witnesses to testify on Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds. /apl

articles.title: Senate allows budget hearings, plenary sessions after morning trials
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate on Wednesday approved a proposal allowing the Committee on Finance and its subcommittees to conduct budget hearings simultaneously with plenary sessions as senators…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate on Wednesday approved a proposal allowing the Committee on Finance and its subcommittees to conduct budget hearings simultaneously with plenary sessions as senators seek to expedite deliberations on the national budget.

This will be the set-up every Monday to Wednesday, 3 p.m. onwards, as the Senate also convenes as an impeachment court every 10 a.m. on those days amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

“Impeachment tayo sa buong umaga… pagkatapos po niyan, legislation na po tayo. Para mapabilis lang po is, we will do legislation here in the Senate plenary session hall, while there will be subsequent subcommittee budget hearings in the different halls of the Senate, including the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC),” Senate Majority Leader Migz Zubiri explained during Wednesday’s plenary session.

(Impeachment proceedings will take place throughout the morning. After that, we will proceed with legislation. To expedite matters, we will conduct legislation here in the Senate plenary session hall, while subsequent subcommittee budget hearings will be held in the Senate’s various halls, including the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC).)
The said arrangement was allowed after Zubiri moved to suspend Senate rules prohibiting committee meetings and hearings while the chamber is in session.
Senate President Win Gatchalian clarified that the exemption would apply only to the Finance Committee and its subcommittees for purposes of budget hearings.
With no objections, Gatchalian then declared the motion approved.

According to Zubiri, the Senate currently has three major priorities to attend to: the impeachment proceedings, the national budget, and legislation. Hence, senators would have to “double time” to accommodate these.
Zubiri clarified that senators who chair the subcommittees conducting the budget hearings will be considered present in the Senate sessions and will not be marked absent.
Minority raises quorum, contentious budget issues

Meanwhile, Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano said the minority bloc was in partial agreement with the arrangement but stressed that it would be subject to regular assessment and the Senate’s quorum rules.
He said that quorum would be particularly important in the passage of certain measures.
“We’ll do Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, then assess if it’s working. I hope it works, and we all will work together [so] that it will work,” Cayetano said.
“But there will be substantial issues, especially with the budget, that I think may become contentious, and I hope we can still continue to work together on those issues,” he added.
In response, Gatchalian said the Senate would evaluate the arrangement every week to determine whether it remained the most efficient setup for the chamber.

During the impeachment trial this Wednesday, presiding officer Sen. Chiz Escudero likewise said the Senate impeachment court is considering holding whole day proceedings for Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, with no plenary sessions starting October until the second regular session of the chamber resumes on November 9.
In addition, he said that there will only be two trial days for the first two weeks of November to make way for budget deliberations. /mr

articles.title: Did hackers hit PH nuclear agency, shipping firm with alleged Navy ties?
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Hunt.io says a Chinese-speaking operator quietly collected sensitive nuclear and personnel data from a nuclear agency, along with WordPress data, media library, and credentials…

items: A US cybersecurity firm, Hunt.io, reported a hack involving the theft of sensitive files from a Philippine nuclear research agency and a shipbuilding company linked to the Navy, allegedly by Chinese-speaking operatives.

The stolen data includes critical information on nuclear materials, safety protocols, personnel details, and strategic plans, with evidence suggesting the attackers used a slow download method to avoid detection.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Did someone just steal sensitive files from a Philippine nuclear research agency, including documents on nuclear materials, radiation safety, government personnel, and security credentials? And did the same operator hack a Philippine shipbuilding company that provides services to the Navy?
That’s what a US cybersecurity company called Hunt.io says it discovered on August 13 in a hack they claim was conducted by Chinese-speaking operatives.
Potentially quite a lot.

Hunt.io claimed to have recovered 176 files totaling 372 megabytes (MB) that it said came from the nuclear research agency, out of a vulnerability from ownCloud, a free and open source software for content collaboration and file sharing that is “commonly deployed by organizations as a self-hosted alternative to commercial cloud storage.”

The vulnerability, as Hacker News explained, is an “authentication bypass that could allow an attacker to access, modify or delete any file without authentication if the username of the victim is known and the victim has no signing-key configured.”
Though the report doesn’t specifically name the targeted agency, the country’s body for nuclear research is the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute under the Department of Science and Technology.

Hunt.io said the stolen information includes data on research reactor core components, historical fuel inventories, radiation safety and incident reporting, and people authorized to interact with equipment, providing “a technical picture of the facility: reactor configuration, movement histories, and the individuals authorized to interact with that equipment.”

There were also strategic plans for 2023 to 2028, IT documents, personal data sheets, Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net worth, curricula vitae (CVs) and résumés, passport-related documents, and employee foreign travel records. ”Strategy documents reveal internal priorities and program direction, which can be valuable to competitors and attackers alike,” Hunt.io said.
Hunt.io also found a KeePass password database, encrypted files, and a BitLocker recovery key.
Many of the files were already arranged in Chinese-labeled folders.

While Hunt.io was able to analyze 372 MB of files, as mentioned above, the total amount of data exfiltrated may be bigger. The company saw a reference to 9 gigabytes (GB) of files that had been marked as exfiltrated but were no longer in the directory.
The researchers also found a 192-MB database dump from a biometrics personnel and attendance system, potentially revealing information about employees and their access patterns.
One of the more interesting clues was hidden in the alleged attacker’s own code.
Scripts used to retrieve files from the nuclear research agency contained comments and descriptions written in Simplified Chinese.
Among them were phrases that translate to “low-speed download of nuclear material documents,” “low-speed download of radiation safety key files,” and “low-speed download of IT planning.”
Why would hackers deliberately download something slowly? Maybe because they didn’t want anyone to notice.

Hunt.io found that the scripts inserted randomized pauses between requests, including gaps of three to six seconds. The researchers believe this was intended to make the traffic less conspicuous and evade detection.
“The heavy use of Chinese in the docstrings, code comments, and output folders strongly suggests the operator is a native speaker, or very comfortable with the language,” the company said.
This, Hunt.io argued, suggests someone wasn’t simply grabbing everything available. The operators appeared to know what information they wanted.
Hunt.io is a Florida-based cybersecurity company whose founders have backgrounds in threat-intelligence company Recorded Future, which Mastercard acquired for $2.65 billion in 2024.

Hunt.io cofounders Chris Ueland and Courtney Couch previously worked on Recorded Future’s attack surface team, while Hunt.io head of product German Hoeffner previously headed vulnerability research there.

More importantly, Hunt.io said it disclosed its findings to the National Computer Emergency Response Team (NCERT) under the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) before publication and held the report until August 25 as part of responsible disclosure. According to Hunt.io, NCERT coordinated notification of the affected organizations.
Rappler has sought confirmation from NCERT, and has also reached out to Hunt.io.
Hunt.io said the operator exploited CVE-2023-49105, a critical ownCloud vulnerability that, under certain conditions, can allow files to be accessed without authentication.
OwnCloud disclosed the vulnerability way back in November 2023.
If Hunt.io’s findings are confirmed, why was a vulnerability, discovered nearly three years earlier, apparently still exploitable?

Here’s another interesting development: two days after Hunt.io published its findings, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also added CVE-2023-49105 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
One of the requirements for a vulnerability to be added to the KEV catalog is that “there is reliable evidence that the vulnerability has been actively exploited in the wild.”
Hunt.io said it also found evidence that a Philippine marine engineering and shipbuilding company that provides services to the Navy had been digitally compromised.

The researchers found 195 MB of allegedly stolen data, including a copy of the company’s WordPress installation, database, and media library. Hunt.io said the operator had obtained credentials and multiple potential ways back into the company’s website.
Whether the compromise reached systems or information connected to the company’s Navy work is unclear.

Hunt.io also does not attribute the attack to Beijing or any known threat group, but only noted that they are Chinese-speaking, and with “medium confidence” that this is a “targeted” hack meant to quietly collect some potentially very sensitive Philippine information.
“The preciseness of the scripts, deliberate organization of stolen data by content, and the nature of the selected data are difficult to reconcile with an opportunistic actor,” it said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Armed men abduct Kenyan editor, employer suspects government
articles.summary: A newspaper editor in Kenya was kidnapped from a car late on Tuesday and then located near a dam far away a few hours later. The Standard paper said it suspected state involvement in an attempt to…

image.caption: Kenyan newspaper The Standard is often crticial of President William Ruto, who singled the paper out in comments online over the summerImage: James Wakibia/SOPA Images/Sipa USA/picture alliance

blocks.text: An associate editor for one of Kenya's largest news outlets, The Standard, was abducted by armed men overnight and then released near a dam far from the scene around nine hours later, his employer said on Wednesday.
Alex Kiprotich was taken from a car at around 9:20 p.m. on Tuesday on a road near the city of Nakuru.

"The circumstances of Mr Kiprotich's abduction remain deeply troubling, and we will continue to press for full accountability," the government-critical outlet said in a press release after his discovery.
Late on Tuesday the Standard Group's CEO Chaacha Mwita had also said that the "abduction bears all the hallmarks of a targeted attack on a journalist for doing his job."

blocks.caption: Kirpotich (left in picture) and CEO Mwita appeared at a Nairobi press confernce on WednesdayImage: Monicah Mwangi/REUTERS

blocks.text: What do we know about the apparent abduction?
The newspaper released a video overnight of what appeared to be dashcam footage from the car Kiprotich was traveling in when he was abducted.

A white vehicle without any markings apparent in the footage came to a stop in front of the car in an area where temporary barriers created a single-lane bottleneck on the Gilgil-Nakuru highway, and put on its hazard lights.

Four men in civilian clothes and obscuring their faces — some holding firearms and others carrying what appeared to be baseball bats — emerged and converged on the car, soon taking a man back to their vehicle and driving off.
On Wednesday, Standard Group said that Kiprotich had been located near a dam more than 200 kilometers (120 miles) southeast the scene of the abduction roughly nine hours earlier.

"Mr Kiprotich was located by a Standard Group team led by the Group CEO Chaacha Mwita at around 6:30 a.m. near Masinga Dam, after being dumped by his captors in the early hours of the morning," it said.

Kiprotic was "safe, though understandably shaken by his ordeal," his employer said. Kiprotich works for newspaper The Standard, a flagship of the wider media group known for its critical coverage of President William Ruto's government.
Rights groups say activists still being abducted in Kenya
Right groups call for investigation, warn of pattern of abductions and intimidation
Police and the government in Kenya did not immediately comment on the incident.

Dozens of government critics and activists have been abducted in Kenya this year alone, according to a report released this week, with the practice becoming more common since widespread anti-government protests in 2024.
Human rights groups have accused state agencies of being responsible, with Standard Group voicing similar suspicions in this case.
Kiprotich had said in June that he narrowly escaped a previous attempt to kidnap him, which came three days after Ruto called out the Standard Group on social media.

Kenya's editors' guild said it was "shocked, outraged and deeply perturbed" by Tuesday's abduction, describing it as "a disturbing escalation in the intimidation and targeting of journalists in Kenya."
Amnesty International Kenya called for an independent investigation, saying the incident raised "serious concerns for media freedom."

articles.title: ‘It always comes around’: fans react to conviction in Tupac Shakur’s murder 30 years later
articles.summary:
Rapper’s supporters reflect on ‘astonishing’ events leading to Duane Davis being found guilty over 1996 fatal shooting

A

blocks.text: A criminal conviction this week in the murder of Tupac Shakur, the first since the rapper was gunned down in 1996, sent shockwaves through his sea of fans who have waited three decades for answers.
Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a former California gang leader, was found guilty of murder on Monday for the role he played in orchestrating the fatal shooting of Shakur.

The case relied on several confessions from Davis, including his 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, in which he described the events of 7 September 1996. Davis said he came up with a plan to retaliate against Shakur after the rapper’s entourage attacked Davis’s nephew in the lobby of the MGM Grand hotel.
Some of Shakur’s legions of fans reflected on what the artist meant to them while expressing bittersweet joy about the long-awaited moment.

As a teenager, Kelly Wilson, 48, was enamored with hip-hop’s boy wonder. (Shakur was just 25 years old when he died.) “There was a lot of depth to him that I just didn’t hear elsewhere,” the Seattle area resident said on Tuesday.

During his life, Shakur faced blowback over lyrics his detractors regarded as glorifying violence or gang culture. But he was also lauded as an inner-city chronicler, whose pen cast unrelenting social critiques of racial inequality, police brutality and other issues of the time.
“I’m as white Irish as you get,” Wilson said, but he connected with Shakur’s overarching philosophy, which Wilson described as: “Speak for the people who don’t have a voice.”
His children grew up steeped in Shakur’s legacy. One of them, 22-year-old Julian Wilson, drew a parallel to Davis’s trial and one of the first songs in Shakur’s discography that he deeply studied.

The music video for Hail Mary, a track he recorded in 1996, begins with a scene where one incarcerated man laments being wrongfully imprisoned. “Revenge has a funny, funny way of setting the score, and when it happens, you will know,” a fellow inmate consoles him.

“That’s always stuck with me. Some things may take time, but it will always come around,” Julian Wilson said. “Even then, they still had faith that justice was going to be served no matter how long it took.”
The elder Wilson felt mixed emotions about Davis’s guilty verdict. “It’s nice to have the final chapter written for the family and those that need that healing,” he said.

At the same time, Wilson called the verdict “long overdue”, adding that others who may have been more culpable have since passed away. (Authorities have long suspected Davis’s nephew, Orlando Anderson, of being the gunman. Anderson died in 2004.)
after newsletter promotion
Casey Rain, a British musician, was a moderator for HitEmUp.com, a forum dedicated to Shakur that was popular in the early aughts.

“I don’t mind admitting that there was a time in the years immediately following his passing where I definitely bought into some of those conspiracy theories. A lot of people did because we didn’t have access to the information that we have now,” Rain said, referencing longstanding fan theories about who killed Shakur, or whether Shakur was secretly still alive.

“Everything surrounding his murder has kind of existed in this middle ground of historical events and folklore. For somebody to be convicted of doing it, that grounds it and makes it real,” he continued. “This isn’t a sort of hip-hop, folklore, mythology story. This is a 25-year-old man that was murdered.”
In the end, Rain was also struck by how the case against Davis relied on his own admissions regarding the deadly night.
“It finally got solved because one of the people involved in it just wouldn’t shut up talking about it. It’s a really strange kind of irony. It’s astonishing,” Rain said.
Davis is set to be sentenced in October. The 63-year-old is facing at least 40 years in prison.

articles.title: Iran accuses US of ‘war crime’ after missile blast kills five people at wedding
articles.summary:
Blast also injures 68 guests at the wedding in southern Iran, prompting fears of escalation in hostilities

Iran has accused the US of a “war crime” after a missile blast killed at least five…

blocks.text: Iran has accused the US of a “war crime” after a missile blast killed at least five people and injured 68 who were attending a wedding at a private home in a coastal city of southern Iran, as the fresh exchange of strikes prompted fears of a wider renewal of hostilities.

Iranian media said that the wedding ceremony was being held in a home in the city of Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, late on Tuesday when a US missile struck, with shrapnel and debris from the strike killing and injuring people.
Among the dead was a four-year-old child, Amir-Ali Karimi, and a 16-year-old, Mohammad Mollahi.
“It’s a terrible thing. I’m extremely worried and upset about what happened – really upset,” Ali Mollahi, the father of the bride, told Mehr News.
The deputy of the provincial government, Ahmad Nafisi, said first responders had headed immediately to the scene and transferred the wounded to the hospitals.
Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson called the US attack a “war crime” and said Iran “will respond to these savage crimes with firmness”.
The chief Iranian negotiator, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, said the attack had killed families with children, and called the US the “great Satan”.
“If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan and kills like Satan, it’s Satan. Shields a junior Satan that does the same? It’s THE Great Satan,” Ghalibaf said in a post on X.

The US attacks on Tuesday ended a month-long uneasy truce between the US and Iran and appeared to signal a resumption of another cycle of escalation. US Central Command (Centcom) said the overnight strikes focused on Iranian military targets including air defence sites, radars and maritime assets.

Iran responded by launching drones and missiles on US bases across the Middle East, including in Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE. Iran’s military spokesperson, Lt Col Ebrahim Zolfaghari, vowed “heavier, broader, and more crushing and devestating” retaliation.

Videos of the aftermath of the strike show a caved-in roof, blown-out windows and ground riddled with debris, as well as walls pockmarked with what appeared to be holes from shrapnel. Footage from a nearby hospital showed women in wedding attire watching as injured children were being treated.

“When we arrived there, an explosion occurred. It was very intense. Bricks, stones and cement hit me in the face and head, and many others were injured,” a child who was injured at the wedding told the state-affiliated Fars news agency.
A spokesperson for Centcom, Tim Hawkins, said the US was aware of reports of civilian casualties, but the “US military never targets civilians, unlike the [Iranian Revolutionary Guards Corps]”.

In February, a strike on an elementary school killed at least 156 people, including more than 120 schoolchildren. Independent investigations concluded that the US likely carried out the strike with the assistance of AI, though the US government said the incident remained under investigation.

Pictures of shrapnel collected at the site of Tuesday’s attack were published on Iranian state media, and appeared to show the internal components of US munitions. Trevor Ball, an independent weapons analyst, identified some of the remnants as belonging to the Standoff Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (Slam-Er) missile, which is made by the US weapons company Boeing. The Slam-Er is a 1,500-pound, GPS-guided missile touted by Boeing to be “extremely accurate.”

It was unclear if the home where the wedding was being held was struck directly, or if a missile hit close to the home and debris from the strike hit the home and its occupants. CCTV footage captured at least six strikes in the area within a minute. A separate strike appeared to hit a communications tower about 150 metres away from the home.

The US has been targeting communications and radar infrastructure along Iran’s coast to try to stop its blockade on the strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint which prior to the US-Iran war was a transit point for at least 20% of the world’s oil supply.

Iran has virtually closed the strait since the start of the Iran war, frustrating the US president, Donald Trump, who is facing a midterm election with expensive gas prices and knock-on inflation across the board.
In recent weeks, the US has focused on trying to degrade Iran’s capacity to strike ships transiting the strait to reopen the waterway for traffic.

articles.title: More than 900 killed in Gaza this year despite ceasefire, Hamas-run health ministry says
articles.summary: The ministry says the total number of people killed in the Strip since 10 October is now more than 1,300, including 301 children.

blocks.text: ByEmma Pengelly and Richard Irvine-BrownBBC Verify
More than 900 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza this year despite the ceasefire, according to latest figures from the territory's Hamas-run Ministry of Health.
It brings the total number of people killed in the Strip since the 10 October ceasefire was declared to more than 1,300, including 301 children, the ministry says.

Hamas and Israel agreed to halt the war after accepting US President Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan. That plan included a suspension of "all military operations, including aerial and artillery bombardment".

Since then, BBC Verify has analysed dozens of videos which show the impact of Israeli strikes on locations including a beachside cafe, tents where displaced people have been sheltering, and a reported funeral procession in central Gaza.
Recent months have been some of the most deadly according to the figures, with more than 100 people recorded killed each month between April and August.
The health ministry attributes the deaths directly to Israeli military action, but does not distinguish between civilians and combatants.
The UN considers the figures reliable, and experts have told BBC Verify that their independent analysis is consistent with the ministry's data.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) disputes the ministry's figures. It told BBC Verify there is "no basis to assume" that all those listed were killed as a result of IDF activity.

It said it operates in "a precise manner to remove threats and protect its troops and Israeli civilians, in accordance with the agreement", and that it works to mitigate any civilian harm "to the greatest extent possible".

At the start of this year Israeli media reported that an Israeli security official acknowledged more than 70,000 people had been killed in the Gaza war, which it said included more than 20,000 combatants.
'Ceasefire in name only'

From the start of the ceasefire agreement on 10 October to the end of that month, the ministry recorded 251 deaths. Since then the deadly Israeli attacks have continued every month. The highest monthly death toll this year was recorded in July, when 152 people were killed including 21 children, according to the figures.
The IDF says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire and one contractor was killed in an "operational accident".
It also says it has killed hundreds of military operatives since October.

Conflict monitoring group Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (Acled), which uses official statements, media reports and social media to verify attacks, says it has recorded around 200 Israeli strikes during the ceasefire that have reportedly killed Hamas operatives or other armed "militants" in targeted strikes.
Acled said this includes commanders involved in planning the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, which triggered the war and killed around 1,200 people with 251 taken hostage.

Hugh Lovatt, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations think tank, said "Gaza has seen a ceasefire in name only" since last October. He said the Israeli military has continued its almost daily air and drone strikes, and "though it claims to be targeting Hamas or imminent threats, it is Gaza's civilians that have continued to bear the brunt".
This could now be a "central stumbling block" in international efforts to implement Trump's ceasefire deal, he added.
The IDF told BBC Verify it "remains committed" to the ceasefire agreement and that there have been "continued violations and threats posed by Hamas and other terror organizations" in Gaza.
Summer of deadly incidents
Warning: The following segment of this story contains graphic content which some readers might find distressing.
Multiple deadly Israeli strikes in Gaza in under 24 hours
BBC Verify has analysed dozens of videos of attacks in Gaza carried out since the ceasefire.

In one, emergency services are seen attending to people in the aftermath of a strike at a beachside cafe in Gaza City on 18 August, where six people were killed, according to the health ministry. The next day nine people, including a 13-year-old, were reportedly killed in a strike on a police headquarters in the al-Tuffah neighbourhood.
The IDF said it was targeting Hamas commanders and terrorists in the two incidents and that "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".

One of the deadliest single incidents in July was a strike on a reported funeral procession in Nuseirat. Seven people were killed and 22 injured, according to the Al-Awda Hospital where casualties were taken. Several verified images show nine people covered in blood lying on the street. Two people appear to still be alive and are being treated by bystanders.
The IDF said it was targeting a "significant military operative" of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group who was involved in the 7 October 2023 attacks.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Men assess scene of Israeli strike on high-rise block in Gaza City on 2 August

blocks.text: Image source, Supplied
Men assess scene of Israeli strike on high-rise block in Gaza City on 2 August

In a strike on an apartment block on the western edge of Gaza City overnight on 1 August, a pregnant woman, her husband and their young son were killed, according to local reports. Verified footage showed the body of an unborn baby in the rubble.

A man searching the ruins said he had heard a strike overnight and saw smoke coming from the building. "I broke the door and went up and I found dead bodies scattered," he said. The IDF said it had targeted an acting Hamas commander.
Child deaths 'absurd and devastating'

UN agency Unicef has also reported more than 300 children have been killed since the ceasefire. The aid organisation has been tracking all available reports of incidents affecting children in Gaza, including via UN personnel on the ground.
James Elder, Unicef global spokesperson, said the number of child deaths was "absurd and devastating".
He added that hundreds more have been injured. "A ceasefire that paints such a grim picture can only be failing children."

Unicef and other humanitarian organisations operating inside Gaza have also reported Israeli strikes on their workers since the ceasefire. This includes two water truck drivers contracted by Unicef killed in April by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza.

The IDF said its soldiers "identified suspects approaching" the Yellow Line area during the incident, who were later identified as UN contractors who had not "coordinated in advance". Unicef said the drivers were carrying out routine water trucking operations with "no changes in movement or procedures".
Aid Worker Security Database, whose figures have been cited by the UN and UK government, told BBC Verify it has recorded 22 aid workers killed in Gaza since 10 October 2025.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Palestinians grieve over bodies of people killed in an Israeli attack targeting a beachfront cafe in Gaza City

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Palestinians grieve over bodies of people killed in an Israeli attack targeting a beachfront cafe in Gaza City

Independent research group Airwars works to identify civilian deaths from a range of open sources including news agencies, NGOs and social media, matching names it finds to those published by the health ministry.
Director Emily Tripp told BBC Verify the ministry's data on death tolls is consistent with its own tracking and research, and that it recorded more than 60 deadly incidents in July.
"This is the highest number of fatal incidents we've seen in a month since the ceasefire," Tripp said. "Our own findings point to an increasing number of civilian harm incidents a month."

Professor Michael Spagat from Royal Holloway, University of London, is the chair of Every Casualty Counts, a charity that studies death tolls in wars. He told BBC Verify that the figures recorded by the health ministry are "testable" because it publishes names, ages and ID numbers of the dead.

He said that since April, the monthly death toll in Gaza has been roughly double what was seen in December. "July was the worst month but even August's lower toll is still high compared with the November to March period," he added.
Additional reporting Paul Brown, Benedict Garman and Lamees Altalebi

articles.title: Rosenberg: Putin's veiled threat to UK part of Russia's campaign against West
articles.summary: The Russian president wants to keep Britain guessing - and stressing - over Moscow's real intentions.

blocks.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin responded with one short sentence when asked at a press conference whether Moscow might strike military facilities in the UK in response to British arms supplies to Ukraine.
"That's a secret. A military secret."
Military secret is not a "yes". And not a "no". It leaves us hanging.
And that, I suspect, is the point.

Those two words feel like psychological pressure from the Kremlin: to keep Britain guessing - and stressing - over Moscow's intentions, as well as to encourage the UK to think twice about its staunch support for Ukraine.

It reminds me of a newspaper article I read a few days ago. Moskovsky Komsomolets had suggested that UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham should be seeing Russia, not in his dreams, "but in his nightmares".
Scary language. But short on detail about what those nightmares will look like.
We cannot conclude that Russian missiles are about to be used against targets in the UK.
But look what's happening elsewhere in Europe.
Germany now says Russia was responsible for last month's drone attack at Leipzig airport.
Putin accused Germany of "planting the evidence". But German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described "the well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe".
Could such "operations" now be stepped up in the UK?
Yet it wasn't just Britain that received veiled threats at Putin's press conference.
So did the West in general. Putin referred to Western countries as sharks.

"If anyone tries to drag us down the food chain, to gobble us up or devour us, they might get punched in the teeth," he said. "Russia is ready to do that, despite the rapidly growing appetites and teeth of these sharks."
Increasingly Russia's president is mixing the geopolitical with the zoological. He recently spoke about killer whales "tearing polar bears apart" to justify Russia's war on Ukraine.
The press conference in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, was a fascinating window on Putin's state of mind.

For forty-five minutes he took questions from Russian journalists and came across as combative, confident of victory and energised. These days Putin appears most animated when talking about the geopolitical standoff between Russia and the West and the war in Ukraine.
Even though the war has not gone to plan. Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield and the country's economy is under considerable pressure.
"I have no doubt that the enemy will crumble," he declared. Yet the war has lasted more than four-and-a-half years and Ukraine fights on.
Officially the Kremlin still calls this a "special military operation". But even Putin now is using the word "war".
"War is a brutal and unpredictable thing," he said at the press conference.
He claimed that he remained open to negotiations to end the conflict and left no doubt with whom he'd prefer to sit down with from the US administration: Donald Trump's envoys.

"We are absolutely comfortable working with those people we know well and generally trust," Putin said. "[Jared] Kushner and [Steve] Witkoff are always welcome guests. It's a pleasure working with them."
There was no such name check for the CIA director who had made a surprise visit to Moscow last week. The Kremlin says the Russian president didn't meet John Ratcliffe during that trip.
Is Putin likely to meet Witkoff and Kushner anytime soon?
There's nothing in the diary. Not yet.
But if they do head to Moscow, President Trump's envoys will encounter a Kremlin leader who remains determined that any peace in Ukraine should be on Russia's terms.

articles.title: PhilHealth to launch Yakap 2.0 with stricter verification process
articles.summary: The Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) is working on the enhanced Yaman ng Kalusugan Program (Yakap 2.0) with improved policies and a stricter verification process, PhilHealth president…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 7:40pm

The Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) is working on the enhanced Yaman ng Kalusugan Program (Yakap 2.0) with improved policies and a stricter verification process, PhilHealth president Beverly Lorraine Ho said Wednesday.
During the House budget hearing, Ho said Yakap 2.0 is the result of its consultation and feedback from various stakeholders.
“We will be coming up with our Yakap 2.0 enhanced policies, and that's a result of all the consultations and all the feedback that's coming from the ground,” Ho said.
Among the improvements are the use of biometrics to verify the actual patient and the inclusion of the healthcare provider claiming on behalf of the patient in the eGov app.

The improvements are being done amid reports that some local government units (LGUs) allegedly used the program for fraudulent activities such as enrolling residents without their knowledge and using the funds for anomalous transactions.
YAKAP is an enhanced primary care benefit package covering consultations, indicated laboratory and cancer screening tests, and even prescribed essential medicines.
Earlier this year, PhilHealth included screening tests for the four top cancers: breast, liver, lung, and colorectal.
YAKAP also offers free consultations, 13 free laboratory procedures, and 75 free medicines. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos: Debris, possible illegal logging clogged Sto. Cristo Dam
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday said the Sto. Cristo Dam in Pampanga was not damaged but became clogged with debris, including logs that may have come from illegal…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday said the Sto. Cristo Dam in Pampanga was not damaged but became clogged with debris, including logs that may have come from illegal logging upstream.
In a statement following his inspection of the dam, Marcos said a temporary barrier would be put up to prevent debris, logs, and other materials from flowing downstream and blocking the dam.

“Hindi naman pala na-damage ‘yung dam. Kung hindi, ang nangyari nabara dahil hindi basura kundi ‘yung debris, mga troso na siguro nagpuputol sila na illegal logging sa taas, bumababa rito, nabara ngayon ‘yung dam, umikot ‘yung tubig,” he said.

(It turned out that the dam itself was not damaged. Rather, it was blocked by debris, including logs that may have come from illegal logging upstream. The debris flowed downstream and clogged the dam, causing the water to divert and flow in another direction.)

“Kaya ‘yung nakita natin na bahay na nahulog, nahulog sa ilog. Dahil nga umiwas na doon sa dam, gumawa ng sariling daanan dito. Sinira ‘yung wall natin kasi galing na sa likod ‘yung tubig. Sinira ‘yung wall dito at dito na dumaan ‘yung tubig,” the President also said.

(That is why the house we saw had fallen into the river. Because the water was diverted away from the dam, it carved out its own path, causing the wall to collapse as the water came from behind it. The water then breached the wall and flowed through that area.)
A video showing the two-story house in Barangay Sta. Rita-Sto. Cristo in Lubao, Pampanga, went viral on social media after raging floodwaters washed away the structure.
Marcos said a Sabo Dam, a structure designed to control sediment and debris in mountain streams and rivers, would be built upstream to prevent similar incidents.

“Lahat ng dam natin ngayon kailangan na natin maglagay ng ganyan sa mga upstream ay lalagyan natin pagka praktikal, kung tama ay lalagyan natin ng Sabo Dam. Kung hindi, ito lang muna, ‘yung mga harang lang muna para hindi mabara ‘yung dam natin para tama ang takbo ng tubig,” he said.

(We now need to install similar measures upstream of all our dams. Where practical and appropriate, we will install Sabo Dams. Otherwise, we will initially put up barriers to prevent debris from clogging the dams and ensure that the water continues to flow properly.)

The inspection was followed by visits to the PAGCOR Multi-Purpose Evacuation Center and the Provincial Evacuation Center and Isolation Facilities, where Marcos checked on families seeking temporary shelter after being displaced by the flooding.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) provided P10,000 in cash assistance to each family, in addition to hygiene, sleeping, and kitchen kits. The families also received family food packs and regular meals.
Marcos’ final stop was the remote and isolated Barangay Santa Fe in San Marcelino, Zambales, where he received a briefing on the situation from national and local government officials. /mr

articles.title: OVP tells House panel Duterte will be absent from budget hearing
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Vice President (OVP) informed the House committee on appropriations that the vice president’s chief of staff – Zuleika Lopez – will be the one to attend…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Vice President (OVP) informed the House committee on appropriations that the vice president’s chief of staff – Zuleika Lopez – will be the one to attend its budget briefing.
Lopez will join the proceeding on behalf of Vice President Sara Duterte,
Palawan 2nd District Rep. Jose Alvarez gave the information on Wednesday.
Alvarez, who serves as the vice chairperson of the House panel, said that Duterte sent a formal letter to the committee that she would not be able to attend the budget briefing on Wednesday.
Duterte was seen attending a mass for the Divine Rostro at the Basilica Minore de Peñafrancia in Naga City on Tuesday.
“They sent a letter that instead of the usual head of office presenting, this team will do it instead,” Alvarez said in an ambush interview after the budget briefing.
The lawmaker explained that Lopez was allowed to attend the agency’s budget hearing as she also serves as the undersecretary.
He noted that only heads of agencies or undersecretaries can defend the budget briefing.
He recalled an instance last year where no official from the OVP showed up for the budget deliberations.
He had advised Duterte’s staff members to skip the hearing since the panel received a letter that an assistant secretary would defend their budget.
Alvarez said that the House panel will just invite Duterte in the plenary-level budget deliberations, at the same time, observing that there are no contentions to the agency’s budget.
During the budget hearing, the OVP was not given parliamentary courtesy to waive questions from lawmakers about its budget.
Bagong Henerasyon Party-list Rep. Robert Nazal made a motion to extend the same courtesy to the OVP the same way the panel did to the Office of the President on Tuesday.
Nazal noted that the request was not made for “special treatment,” but for “consistency that this committee treats every co-equal branch of government to the same measure of respect and fairness.”
However, ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio objected to the motion, emphasizing that such courtesy must be abolished by the Congress to uphold transparency and accountability in budget talks.
Alvarez then recognized both motion and objection, and asked the resource persons if they could answer questions about the budget only, in which Lopez agreed to do so.
In the separate interview, Alvarez noted that the panel would be free to ask any question if there is no ongoing impeachment trial for Duterte.
“I told them to confine their questions regarding the budget presentation because there is an ongoing trial,” he noted. /apl

articles.title: Manila Water expands network to 5,738 km to boost East Zone service
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Manila Water continues to expand its water distribution network to bring 24/7 water service to more customers across the East Zone of Metro Manila and Rizal. As of July, the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Manila Water continues to expand its water distribution network to bring 24/7 water service to more customers across the East Zone of Metro Manila and Rizal. As of July, the company’s network spans 5,738.06 kilometers of pipelines, supporting the delivery of safe and reliable water to millions of customers in its service area.

Serving more than 7.9 million customers and growing, Manila Water continues to invest in expanding and upgrading its water distribution network to meet increasing demand and improve service reliability. These ongoing infrastructure investments help ensure that safe and reliable water reaches households, businesses, and communities throughout the East Zone while supporting future growth.

Maintaining this extensive network requires a sustained focus on leak prevention and the reduction of illegal connections to ensure that more water reaches customers. As of July, Manila Water’s year-to-date non-revenue water level stood at 14.24%, among the lowest in Asia.

“As part of our service improvement and water security programs, we at Manila Water continuously implement long-term initiatives designed to reach more customers while ensuring uninterrupted 24/7 water service for our growing customer base,” said Manila Water Corporate Communications Group Head Dittie Galang.

The company’s network expansion is supported by its long-term strategy to develop additional raw water sources and reduce dependence on Angat Dam. Over the years, Manila Water has diversified its water supply portfolio through facilities such as the 100-million-liter-per-day (MLD) Cardona Water Treatment Plant and the 50 MLD East Bay Phase 1 Water Treatment Plant, both of which draw water from Laguna Lake. Also under development is the East Bay Phase 2 Water Treatment Plant, which is expected to supply up to 200 MLD.

Further strengthening water security is the Wawa-Calawis Water Supply System in Antipolo City, which sources raw water from the 710 MLD Upper Wawa Dam. The system is supported by downstream facilities, including the 80 MLD Calawis Water Treatment Plant and the upcoming 220 MLD Kaysakat Water Treatment Plant.

blocks.text: Teamsters union leaders support Republicans despite members endorsing Democratic candidates
Michael Sainato
The powerful Teamsters union is backing Republican candidates in the 2026 election cycle even after members have voted to support their Democrat opponents.
The 1.3 million-strong union’s president, Sean O’Brien, angered many members and union leaders in 2024 when he became the first union president to speak at the Republican national convention (RNC).
The latest moves by the union’s leadership are further stoking tensions within the union.

“The Republicans have done nothing but take a gun to our head at every turn. And why we think that we can somehow change their behavior, I don’t understand it. It’s not a logical argument,” said John Palmer, who was elected on O’Brien’s slate in 2021 as an at-large vice-president on the Teamsters executive board, but who broke ranks in criticizing O’Brien’s RNC appearance in 2024. “I live in Texas. I’m a moderate guy, but I know when somebody’s trying to cut my throat.”

The national union declined to make an endorsement in the 2024 presidential election for the first time since 1996, claiming a majority of members supported Trump after they supported Biden in 2020, though Teamsters locals and councils representing 1 million members at the union independently endorsed Harris.
So far this election cycle, O’Brien has made two personal contributions – both to Republicans.
O’Brien donated $1,000 to the Republican US Senate campaign of Scott Brown in New Hampshire on 19 February 2026. Brown appeared on O’Brien’s podcast, Better Bad Ideas, on 25 February.

The only Teamsters’ local in New Hampshire, Teamsters Local 633, endorsed Brown’s Democratic rival Chris Pappas for the Senate race in April 2025. Teamsters Local 633 did not respond to multiple requests for comment.
Trump nominates loyalist Hung Cao to be permanent navy secretary amid increased attacks on Iran
Hello and welcome to the US live politics blog.
Donald Trump has picked acting navy secretary Hung Cao to take on the job permanently amid concerns that some sailors have been stretched to the limit during his Iran war.
“I am pleased to nominate a true WARRIOR,” Trump wrote on social media, pushing the Senate “to confirm this Warfighter, ASAP.”

Cao has been serving as acting navy secretary since John Phelan departed the job unexpectedly and without explanation in late April. Unlike Phelan, who had not served in the military or had a civilian leadership role in the service, Cao spent 25 years in the navy as a special operations officer and went on to serve with Seal teams and special forces in Iraq and Afghanistan.
Cao on social media called it the “honor of a lifetime to lead the great warriors of the Navy and Marine Corps team”.

Cao’s nomination comes as some, including Democrats in Congress, believe Trump has been overtaxing the navy. The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier’s nine-month deployment to support the Iran war has included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea.

It comes as Iran launched a wave of attacks on US sites across the Middle East, with violence surging after an extensive American bombardment. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards announced attacks on US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, in the six-month conflict’s heaviest exchange in weeks.
Trump had warned earlier of “much harder and higher” attacks if Iran retaliated to the US strikes, which Iran’s military and state media said killed 18 people.
The renewed attacks deepen the impasse in the war, where Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strait of Hormuz oil export route with the US pressing a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
In other developments:

items: Senator Ed Markey won the Democratic primary in Massachusetts, beating back a challenge from Seth Moulton, who argued his opponent was too old to be effective at his job. Progressive lawmakers and the organization Our Revolution hailed the victory.

Democratic leaders in the US House sharply criticized two representatives for defecting and joining with Republicans in order to advance a procedural vote, describing it as a “significant breach of trust,” that requires “a serious response”.

The US House of Representative voted to censure Chuck Edwards, a Republican congressman who the ethics committee found violated rules against sexual harassment in his conduct towards two young female staffers.

The Trump administration seized on House Democrats voting against a resolution denouncing socialism, condemning the lawmakers as “sick [and] dangerous”. The resolution included language calling for the enactment of Trump’s SAVE America Act, a strict voting bill that would ban mail-in ballots and require voters to prove their citizenship.
Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, criticized Donald Trump for withholding $87m in counter-terrorism funds from the state, describing the move as a betrayal of 9/11 victims.
Donald Trump’s Department of Homeland Security has apparently taken steps to advance the president’s efforts to limit voting.

articles.title: Madagascar ex-Senate chief sentenced to hard labour over deadly Gen Z protest crackdown
articles.summary: At least 22 people were killed and more than 100 injured during last year's unrest, according to the UN.

blocks.text: The protests began a year ago, initially sparked by anger over persistent power and water shortages, before developing into a broader movement against Rajoelina's government.
At least 22 people were killed and more than 100 injured during the unrest, according to UN figures cited by local media.
The protests eventually triggered a political crisis that led to Rajoelina's removal from power and the installation of a new administration led by Col Michael Randrianirina.
The crackdown was led by the gendarmerie, where Ravalomanana retained considerable influence at the time.
He "directed violent actions to suppress the demonstrations", a state prosecutor said in December 2025.
Ravalomanana was removed as Senate president in October, shortly after the protests, and was arrested at his home in December after failing to respond to a summons from the gendarmerie.
He was later placed in pre-trial detention at the high-security Imerintsiatosika prison outside Antananarivo, where he has spent the past seven months.

He is among several senior figures associated with Rajoelina's former government who have faced legal proceedings since the change of power. Ravalomanana is also facing a separate corruption investigation.

A former national police chief who testified at the trial backed his account, saying Ravalomanana was not part of the operational chain of command and had issued no orders to police, gendarmes or soldiers deployed during the unrest.
His lawyer questioned the evidence linking him directly to the violence.
"Is there confirmed written or verbal evidence... to accuse him?" he asked the court, arguing that prosecutors had failed to produce proof that security officers had received orders from his client.
Ravalomanana's defence team said it would challenge the verdict in a higher court.
The court dropped a separate allegation of making a death threat after ruling that the case was too old to prosecute.
Known for wearing a cowboy hat and displaying his military medals, Ravalomanana was viewed by protesters as a symbol of authoritarian power.

articles.title: Long-tailed macaque retrieved after attacking child in Zamboanga del Sur
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Environmental authorities here have taken custody of a Philippine long-tailed macaque (Macaca fascicularis philippensis) after it reportedly attacked a child…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Environmental authorities here have taken custody of a Philippine long-tailed macaque (Macaca fascicularis philippensis) after it reportedly attacked a child in Barangay Upper Pulacan, Labangan , Zamboanga del Sur.
The Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) – Ramon Magsaysay retrieved the primate last August 25 following a report from resident Ireneo Mangubat.

CENRO officer Expedito Flores said Wednesday, Sept. 2, that Mangubat contacted authorities immediately after residents captured the animal to facilitate its proper turnover, citing concerns over public safety.

Initial assessments indicated that the macaque was previously domesticated. Rescuers discovered a tether bound around its body, suggesting the animal was a kept pet that had managed to escape. The identity of the owner remains unknown.

The retrieved primate is currently under the care of the Regional Wildlife Rescue Center in Barangay Baclay, Tukuran town, where it is undergoing health assessment, rehabilitation, and disposition evaluation.

CENRO-Ramon Magsaysay said it continues to coordinate with local residents to identify who illegally kept the animal. Officials are also ramping up information drives regarding Republic Act 9147, or the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.
The Philippine long-tailed macaque is classified as an “Other Threatened Species” under Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Administrative Order No. 2004-15.
Under RA 9147, the unauthorized collection, poaching, or keeping of threatened wildlife species carries strict penalties, including fines and imprisonment. /mr
