articles.title: NBI: P63-M counterfeit luxury clothes seized in Pasay, Valenzuela
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Around P63 million worth of counterfeit luxury clothes were confiscated from six mall stalls in Baclaran, Pasay City, and a warehouse in Valenzuela City on Tuesday, according to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Around P63 million worth of counterfeit luxury clothes were confiscated from six mall stalls in Baclaran, Pasay City, and a warehouse in Valenzuela City on Tuesday, according to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI).

In an interview with reporters on Wednesday, NBI’s National Capital Region (NCR) regional director Emeterio Dongallo Jr. said the seized items of clothes imitating two popular sports brands totalled more than 30,000 pieces.
He said the operation began after a law office sought the bureau’s help to investigate the alleged sale of fake luxury clothes in the two Metro Manila cities.

“I immediately tapped my operatives to conduct surveillance in several malls somewhere in Pasay and a warehouse in Valenzuela. So indeed, it is proven na mayroon talagang violation ng infringement,” he said.
(I immediately tapped my operatives to conduct surveillance in several malls somewhere in Pasay and a warehouse in Valenzuela. So indeed, it is proven that there is a violation of the infringement.)

After securing a certification from the brand owners regarding the counterfeit products and conducting test buys, the NBI-NCR applied for search warrants at the Regional Trial Courts of Pasay City and Valenzuela City.
When the courts granted the requests, operatives immediately conducted the search throughout Tuesday.
According to Dongallo, investigation revealed that the seized clothes were being sold for only around P250, which is three times lower than the prices of the original brands.
“On its face, mukhang original itong mga ito. Kapag hinawakan mo lang at sinuri mo ang quality, talagang counterfeit,” he explained.
(On its face, these look original. But when you touch them and check the quality, they are actually counterfeit.)
Dongallo said the fake products are currently being examined, noting that the test results will be used to file charges against the manufacturers, store owners, and others involved.
He added that the individuals who will be found involved in the modus operandi would face charges on violations of the Trade Infringement Act.
The NBI-NCR regional director advised the public to be vigilant when buying products, especially at the start of the Christmas season.
“Kapag sobrang mura, magtaka na tayo, malamang counterfeit yun,” he said.
(If it’s too cheap, we should be surprised; it’s probably counterfeit.) /mr

articles.title: Caraga cops plant trees to mark Crime Prevention Week
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY, Agusan del Norte — Police and other government personnel, students and environmental advocates planted trees in a village here on Tuesday, Sept. 1n, as part of the observance of National…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY, Agusan del Norte — Police and other government personnel, students and environmental advocates planted trees in a village here on Tuesday, Sept. 1n, as part of the observance of National Crime Prevention Week.

The Police Regional Office-13 (PRO-13), led by regional director Brig. Gen. Rolindo Suguilon, organized the activity in Sitio Matin-ao, Barangay Bonbon, in partnership with the Regional Advisory Group for Police Transformation and Development (RAGPTD-13) and other stakeholders.
The activity carried the theme, “Strengthening Civilian Oversight and Collective Action for Safer Communities.”

Among those who joined were National Police Commission-13 director Josephmar Gil, RAGPTD-13 chairperson Ryan Anthony Culima, Barangay Bonbon chairperson Soledad Caralde, and representatives from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources in Region 13 or Caraga region.

Personnel from the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, Bureau of Fire Protection, Philippine Coast Guard, and Armed Forces of the Philippines also participated, along with students from local schools.
Suguilon said the activity highlighted the role of communities and various sectors in both environmental protection and the promotion of public safety.
“Let this activity remind us that meaningful change does not always begin with big things. Sometimes, it begins with something as simple as planting a tree,” Suguilon said. /mr

items: Gilas Pilipinas aims to compensate for its lack of size in the Asian Games by focusing on a fast-paced game under head coach Tim Cone.
The team features a revamped roster with only three players from the previous Asian Qualifiers, as key players like June Mar Fajardo will not participate.
Preparations are underway with tuneup games in South Korea before heading to Japan, and there is hope for the return of naturalized player Justin Brownlee, who is recovering from injuries.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – What Gilas Pilipinas may lack in size in its Asian Games title defense, it hopes to make up for in speed.

Head coach Tim Cone envisions a fast-paced game as the national team parades a rejigged roster for the quadrennial showpiece, a stark contrast to the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers lineup anchored by twin towers Kai Sotto and AJ Edu.
Even June Mar Fajardo, a member of the 2023 championship squad, will not see action in the continental spectacle to be held in Nagoya, Japan, as he retired from national team duty.

Only three players from the Asian Qualifiers team are part of the Asian Games crew, with RJ Abarrientos, Justine Baltazar, and Justin Arana joined by Robert Bolick, Sedrick Barefield, Adrian Nocum, Don Trollano, Zavier Lucero, Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser, Brandon Bates, and Jerrick Ahanmisi in an all-PBA lineup.

“It’s a different system. They’re not playing my system. They’re playing a different system, more of an uptempo, push-the-ball [style], because they’re a little bit smaller. Obviously, they’re smaller because they don’t have Kai and AJ and June Mar playing,” said Cone.
“They’re smaller, so they’re going to use their speed and quickness to get up and down the floor. It will be really interesting to watch.”
Cone and Gilas Pilipinas are ramping up their preparations as they flew to South Korea on Wednesday, September 2, to face its national team in a pair of tuneup games.

Then, from Korea, the Nationals will travel to Japan for the Asian Games, with the men’s basketball tournament running from September 10 to 20, ahead of the official event dates from September 19 to October 4.
Despite the short buildup, Cone likes what he has seen so far from the team, which will go up against China, Bahrain, and Kazakhstan in the group stage.
“The idea of bringing fresher guys, motivated guys, guys who are motivated to come out and play for their country, I think it’s a good idea,” said Cone.
“From what I’ve seen from that team, they’re a lot of fun to watch. I think the fans and the countrymen are going to have a lot of fun watching that team.”
Cone also has his fingers crossed that Justin Brownlee will be healthy enough to join the team, as the coaching staff reserved the 12th roster spot for the naturalized star.

Brownlee, who starred in 2023 as Gilas Pilipinas won its first Asian Games gold medal since 1962, continues to recover from knee and leg injuries that kept him out of the last three games in the Asian Qualifiers.
“We’ve opened up a spot for Justin. We’ll see if he ends up showing up,” said Cone. – Rappler.com

articles.title: DOH assures enough leptospirosis medicine amid surge in cases
articles.summary: DOH assures enough leptospirosis medicine amid surge in cases The Department of Health (DOH) on Wednesday assured the public that it has sufficient medicines to treat leptospirosis patients amid the…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 7:21pm

The Department of Health (DOH) on Wednesday assured the public that it has sufficient medicines to treat leptospirosis patients amid the surge in cases following the continuous torrential rain caused by the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).
During the House budget hearing, DOH Secretary Edwin Mercado said the agency has already distributed leptospirosis medicines across the country before the start of the wet season.

“Meron po tayong download na preemptively even before the start of the rainy season, and then we have at least 3.1 million capsules still in the central warehouse, which is enough buffer for the rest of the year,” Mercado said.
(We have preemptively downloaded even before the start of the rainy season, and we still have at least 3.1 million capsules in the central warehouse, which is enough buffer for the rest of the year.)
For 2027, DOH has allocated P9.76 million to procure 4.88 million capsules of medicine to treat leptospirosis.

“For 2027, we have P9.76 million [and] we will procure 4.88m capsules, so we are prepositioning across the CHD (Center for Health Development) earlier. Again, this will be part of our early procurement,” Mercado said.

In a Balitanghali interview, Dr. Marc Steven Capungcol, chief of the DOH Health Emergency Management Bureau, said DOH hospital in Metro Manila have 77 beds available for leptospirosis patients, with active patient referrals and redistribution in place to prevent overcrowding.
Currently, there are 526 admissions and 33 pending admissions of leptospirosis patients in DOH hospitals in Metro Manila.
According to Capungcol, leptospirosis cases and deaths are 19% lower than those recorded during the same period last year.
The DOH official urged the public to immediately consult a doctor instead of waiting for symptoms of leptospirosis to worsen before seeking medical attention. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: House OKs on final reading PAL’s 50-year franchise extension
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved on final reading a bill extending the Philippine Airlines’ (PAL) franchise to operate as the nation’s flag carrier for another…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The House of Representatives on Wednesday approved on final reading a bill extending the Philippine Airlines’ (PAL) franchise to operate as the nation’s flag carrier for another 50 years.

With 250 lawmakers voting in favor, three against and one abstaining, the chamber passed on final reading House Bill No. 10545, which extends PAL’s franchise to run air-transport services in the Philippines and abroad to 2076, ahead of its expiry in 2028.
Founded in 1941, PAL is among Asia’s oldest commercial carriers, and has since grown into one of the country’s leading airliners.

Last week, the bill’s sponsor, Negros Occidental Rep. Jeffrey Ferrer, told the floor that extending PAL’s legislative franchise will provide it with “the certainty and confidence” needed to undertake long-term investments to boost its services, including expanding its fleet to grow domestic and international routes.

“In turn, this stability can help fuel tourism, facilitate trade and commerce and contribute to exclusive economic growth while reinforcing the Philippines’ position as a competitive player in the international aviation industry,” he said. /mr

articles.title: House bill on 5-year term for barangay, SK officials advances
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A House bill setting the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials to five years was passed on second reading on Wednesday, Sept. 2. This came after lawmakers…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A House bill setting the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials to five years was passed on second reading on Wednesday, Sept. 2.
This came after lawmakers debated over whether the term extension is necessary amid the upcoming barangay and SK elections during the House plenary session on Tuesday.
House Bill No. 10971, also known as an act fixing the term of office of Barangay and SK officials to five years, seeks to amend Republic Act No. 12232, which stipulates a four-year term.

During the interpellation of the bill at the House plenary session on Wednesday, Negros Occidental Rep. Javier Miguel Benitez proposed to cut the three term limit to two years instead, while still pushing for the five-year period of service.

“My amendment is plain: cut the consecutive term limit for barangay officials from three terms to two. If we give our barangay officials five years instead of three, we should ask for something in return— a longer runway to govern, a shorter leash to cling to power,” he said.
He said that the measure ensures that officials in their third year will be barred from running in the next election, while the one-term limit for SK officials will remain unchanged.

“Ang narinig po natin kahapon, is that you fear entrenchment. Here’s your chance to vote against it. Kung tunay na takot tayo sa hari-harian sa barangay, ito ang boto laban dito: sampung taon, hindi labinlimang taon,” Benitez said.

(“What we heard yesterday was a concern about the entrenchment of power. Here is your chance to vote against it. If we are truly afraid of barangay officials acting like petty kings, this is the vote against that: ten years, not fifteen,”)
Benitez, moreover, introduced a new section to the bill, which pertains to the funding of its implementation shall be included in the General Appropriations Act.
He said that the unused funds “shall be deemed continuing appropriation” of the Commission on Elections and may be used in the preparations of the 2028 national and local elections. /gsg

articles.title: MMDA targets 5 rain catchment facilities by first half of 2027
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Wednesday said it is eyeing the completion of the first five rain catchment facilities in the National Capital Region by…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Wednesday said it is eyeing the completion of the first five rain catchment facilities in the National Capital Region by the first half of 2027.

Speaking at a Palace briefing, MMDA Chair Romando “Don” Artes said the facilities will be located at Camp Aguinaldo, Miriam College, and the University of the Philippines (UP) Sunken Garden in Quezon City, as well as Remedios Circle and Rajah Sulayman in the City of Manila.
Rain catchment facilities collect, filter, and store rainwater from roofs or open ground for later use or flood control.

“Iyong five priority projects na ipi-present po namin kay ES [Executive Secretary Ralph Recto] this Thursday lima lang po iyong ipi-present namin na tingin namin kaya namin tapusin by June 2027 pero the rest po nitong 39 kung masisimulan po I think we can finish naman po within the year by December 2027,” said Artes.

(The five priority projects that we will present to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto this Thursday are the five projects that we believe we can complete by June 2027. As for the remaining 39 projects, if we can start them soon, I think we can complete them within the year, by December 2027.)
The feasibility study for the application of nature-based solutions in Metro Manila covering a total of 39 rain catchment sites has already been completed, he said.

“Iyong Haskoning mismo ang nag-determine na ito pong 39 sites na ito again out of 107 iyong napili dahil ito po ay efficient at makakatulong po talaga sa pagma-manage ng baha doon po sa lugar kung saan sila itatayo,” the MMDA chair said.

(Haskoning itself determined that these 39 sites, again selected from the 107 submitted sites, were the most efficient and would genuinely help manage flooding in the areas where they will be constructed.)
Haskoning is an international consulting engineering firm that provides design, planning, and sustainability solutions for the built and natural environment.
Artes said the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has committed a $200-million loan to the government for the project.
He also said the sites were selected with the help of local government units (LGUs), which identified areas prone to flooding and locations where the facilities could potentially be built. /mr

articles.title: PNP to provide support to family of cop shot dead in Batangas
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Wednesday said it will provide assistance to the family of the slain police officer who died attempting to apprehend a robbery suspect in…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Wednesday said it will provide assistance to the family of the slain police officer who died attempting to apprehend a robbery suspect in Balayan, Batangas, during a follow-up operation.

Police Staff Sgt. Von Rico Macuha, who was assigned to the Sta. Teresita Municipal Police Station, died after sustaining a gunshot to the head while trying to pursue the suspect who fled from his temporary residence during the operation.

“We deeply mourn the loss of Police Staff Sergeant Von Rico Bibaño Macuha, who made the ultimate sacrifice while performing his duty. His courage and dedication to protecting the public will always be remembered by the Philippine National Police,” PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said.

“Our deepest condolences go to the family, loved ones, and colleagues of police staff sergeant Macuha. The PNP will stand by his family and ensure that they receive the assistance and benefits due to him as a police officer who died in the line of duty,” he added.
The suspect in Macuha’s death was identified as Carlo Arcilla Sape, who was also already wanted in connection with a robbery case in Barangay Sampaga on Aug. 30.
According to the initial investigation, the authorities have launched a pursuit operation to locate Sape after he left his temporary shelter.
When authorities encountered him, Sape allegedly fired at the officers, hitting Macuha and killing him on the spot with a gunshot wound to the head.

The Batangas Police Provincial Office, meanwhile, has already deployed its Provincial Police Intelligence Unit and Provincial Mobile Force Company for a continuous hot-pursuit operation to determine the suspect’s location. /mr

articles.title: Haze continues to blanket Bohol; air quality becomes ‘acutely unhealthy’
articles.summary: TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Haze continued to blanket parts of Bohol on Wednesday as smoke from forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect the region, raising concerns over worsening air quality.…

blocks.text: TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Haze continued to blanket parts of Bohol on Wednesday as smoke from forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect the region, raising concerns over worsening air quality.
Residents observed thicker haze in several areas, with some wearing face masks while outdoors as a precaution against smoke and dust.
Among them was Catherine Selma, who has asthma.
“I do it to protect myself from smoke and dust,” Selma said.
The haze also continued to obscure views of some parts of the province, including Panglao Island and the mountains of Maribojoc, two of Bohol’s well-known landmarks.

As of 3 p.m. Wednesday, the Environmental Management Bureau Region VII (EMB-7) continued to closely monitor local ambient air quality to assess the presence, extent and potential health impacts of the reported haze across the region.
The Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 215, classified as “acutely unhealthy.”
Under this classification, people are advised to limit outdoor exertion. Those with heart or respiratory diseases, including asthma, are advised to stay indoors and rest as much as possible.
The public was also advised to postpone unnecessary trips and remain cautious when going outdoors.
Depending on conditions, authorities may restrict motor vehicle use and curtail certain industrial activities to help reduce exposure and emissions.
Residents are encouraged to stay informed and regularly check the latest official air quality updates and advisories from EMB Region VII.
Authorities continue to monitor the situation as haze persists over parts of Bohol and other areas in the region. /mr

articles.title: Visayas power trouble persists as grid stays under red alert
articles.summary: CEBU CITY — The power crisis in the Visayas is far from over with the grid falling under red alert anew Wednesday despite the return of several generating units. The National Grid Corporation of the…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY — The power crisis in the Visayas is far from over with the grid falling under red alert anew Wednesday despite the return of several generating units.
The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) on Wednesday placed the Visayas grid under red alert from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. and again from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m.
Grid operators also issued yellow alerts covering 1 p.m. to 3 p.m, 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. to 10 p.m.
Red alert means both power supply and reserves can no longer meet demand, and distributors may implement manual load dropping schemes such as rotational brownouts to prevent total grid collapse.
The latest alert came even as two major power plants in Cebu have returned to service, adding much-needed capacity to the strained grid.
Renante Sevilla, director of the Department of Energy (DOE) Visayas Field Office, said the agency hoped the power situation would improve this month.
But he warned that supply remained vulnerable amid high demand and limited power imports from Mindanao.
“We’re hoping for an improved power situation in the Visayas this month,” Sevilla told reporters.
Unit 2 of Therma Visayas Inc. (TVI) in Toledo City, Cebu has been fully restored after months of repairs, adding 169 megawatts (MW) to the grid.
The KEPCO-SPC Power Corp. facility in Naga City, Cebu, which has a capacity to generate 103 MW of energy, also returned online on Aug. 30, Sevilla said.
But the additional capacity has yet to provide enough cushion for the region’s growing electricity demand.
“While there has been additional supply in the Visayas, our demand remains very high,” Sevilla said. “That’s why we’re hoping for the other unit of TVI to return soon.”
In May 2026, two units at TVI, situated in Toledo City, Cebu, underwent an emergency shutdown due to a suspected boiler tube leak.
As a result, over 300 MW of power, enough to energize up to 300,000 homes, has been stripped off the Visayas grid.
In August alone, the Visayas grid had been placed under red alerts at least 13 times.
DOE-Visayas is also counting on battery energy storage systems to provide additional support to the grid, with more capacity expected to be connected before the end of the year. /mr

articles.title: Health chief awaits DOH bureau’s proposal on $10M PH pledge to WHO
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Health Secretary Edwin Mercado is expecting to receive a recommendation from his department’s Bureau of International Health Cooperation (BIHC) on its US$10 million pledge to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Health Secretary Edwin Mercado is expecting to receive a recommendation from his department’s Bureau of International Health Cooperation (BIHC) on its US$10 million pledge to the World Health Organization (WHO).

“The direction I gave is [to] focus first on local needs,” Mercado told lawmakers when asked by Iloilo 1st District Rep. Janette Garin at the House appropriations committee hearing on the DOH’s 2027 budget.
“We are waiting for the recommendation of the BIHC on how to move forward and also align with the directive that we will be focusing more on local needs,” he said.
The DOH made the $10-million pledge in 2024 to support WHO’s 14th General Program of Work, which is a “strategic document that sets a high-level roadmap and agenda for [its] work on global health.”
The pledge was set to be given to the WHO in tranches of US$2.5 million from 2025 to 2028.
Also at the hearing, Health Undersecretary and BIHC Director Maylene Beltran confirmed that half of the pledge, or US$5 million, had already been given to the WHO so far.
She justified the investment, saying “We do recognize that we need to also create our leadership in the international community.”
Upon questioning by Garin, Beltran committed to providing a list of how the US$5 million given to the international body had been spent.
“Perhaps, you can not spend that anymore and use it on your other needs,” Garin suggested, referring to the remaining amount in the pledge.
Beltran also confirmed that the DOH had proposed P167.2 million under its 2027 budget as part of the commitment to WHO.
Garin, a former health secretary, previously questioned the deal during the committee-level deliberations for the DOH budget last year.
She had asked then-Health Secretary Teodoro Herbosa whether he could realign the proposed funds for the pledge toward his department’s local projects.
Herbosa stepped down from his post last July. /apl

articles.title: Telus accused of misleading B.C. consumer watchdog in probe sparked by mistaken $1,400 cancellation fee
articles.summary: B.C.'s consumer watchdog is locked in a court battle with Telus after accusing the telecommunications giant of stonewalling an inspector trying to determine if a mistaken $1,435.65 contract…

image.caption: Telus has gone to B.C. Supreme Court in a bid to overturn a fine and compliance order from B.C.'s consumer protection watchdog. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: B.C.'s consumer watchdog is locked in a court battle with Telus after accusing the telecommunications giant of stonewalling an inspector trying to determine if a mistaken $1,435.65 cancellation fee was part of a systemic issue.

According to documents obtained by CBC News, Consumer Protection B.C. (CPBC) claimed Telus provided misleading information in response to a request for copies of complaints Telus first insisted did not exist — only to later admit the files were too numerous to sift through.

items: 'Absolutely crushed': Inside the investigation that saw StubHub refund 'devastated' Taylor Swift fans

blocks.text: Last month, Telus appealed to B.C. Supreme Court for a judicial review of an order demanding more than $40,000 in fines and legal fees along with an improvement in how the company responds to regulatory requests and identifies records.

The penalty followed more than a year of back-and-forth between CPBC and both internal and external lawyers for Telus; they accused an agency inspector of overstepping his mandate by issuing what the company considered "illegal" orders for a "fishing expedition."

CBC News obtained records of the investigation through a freedom of information request to the provincial regulator. The documents detail an underlying conflict over the extent of the regulator's right to demand corporate accountability on behalf of frustrated citizens.
"Telecommunications is comprehensively regulated by the federal government," Telus lawyer Julia Won wrote in an email to inspector Jason McColl.

"It is not a good use of public or private resources to engage in investigations of matters already addressed in detail by an industry-specific regulatory regime that also includes investigation and enforcement powers."
'Can you please provide an explanation?'
The case highlights a complaint-resolution landscape that can be confusing for customers of telecommunication companies.

The federal Commission for Complaints for Telecom-Television Services resolves service complaints, but CPBC's mandate includes investigations into alleged violations of B.C.'s Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act (BPCPA) — including contract breaches.

Under those terms, McColl claimed CPBC had a right to initiate an investigation into Telus in January 2025 after receiving a complaint from a customer who claimed she had cancelled a sales contract "but that it was not cancelled."
"It is our understanding that Telus is headquartered in British Columbia, as evidenced in Telus contracts," McColl wrote.

"If this is correct, it means that all Telus contracts (not only the ones with British Columbia based customers) must be in compliance with the BCPCA, notwithstanding that a consumer to a contract may be situated outside of British Columbia."

The records obtained by CBC News do not include a copy of the complaint itself, but at one point McColl asked about a timeframe that saw the woman receive a cancellation notice on Christmas Eve of 2024 along with a "fee of $1,435.65 for said cancellation."
"Can you please provide an explanation for why this fee occurred?" McColl asked.
'We do not have records'

Telus responded to McColl's initial query within weeks, insisting the issue was an isolated incident, cancelling the fee and blaming "human error or misunderstanding by an agent" who continued charging for a service they had been asked to cancel.
But instead of wrapping up his probe, McColl used the complaint as a springboard to open a new inspection.
"We noticed some potential issues of non-compliance with contract provisions under the Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act," he told Won.
"We appreciate your position that there is no systemic issue and our inspection will look to confirm this."

As part of the new investigation, McColl issued an order requiring Telus to disclose copies of all records relating to consumer requests to cancel contracts because they did not meet the terms of the consumer protection legislation.
He also asked for records of "penalty payments demanded and/or collected ... from a consumer seeking to cancel a contract."

Won insisted that Telus did not capture data or make records based on a consumer's request to cancel a contract because it didn't meet the terms of the BCPCA or because goods or services were not supplied within a specific time period.
"We do not have records that respond to your request," Won wrote.

"To be clear, we do not impose 'penalties' on consumers. [Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission] regulations do not allow penalties, but do permit an 'early cancellation fee' under specific circumstances."
'There are thousands of complaint files'

According to the email exchanges, McColl later tested those claims by providing Telus details of a complaint from a customer in Coquitlam, B.C., which he claimed fit the exact parameters of the inspection order.
He then demanded to know why the complaint wasn't located through the company's own searches.
In an email, Won accused McColl of testing Telus and said the company had "deep concerns about the nature of these inquiries."
"Nothing in the Act contemplates that an inspector may run tests of this nature," she wrote.

"We reiterate our request that we focus on actual consumer issues and complaints. If consumers are bringing complaints to your office, we want to know about them ... However opaque general fishing expeditions do not allow for those discussions."
In the aftermath of that exchange, an external lawyer for Telus wrote an email to McColl blaming technical issues relating to "the capacity and scope of electronic searches" for the lack of records.

"As you can appreciate, in a company with millions of customers, there are a vast number of customer communications. TELUS applied certain filters to identify the files most likely to contain responsive communications," the email reads.

"There are thousands of complaint files over the time period referred to in your demand for information. [There are] far too many records to review manually to assess whether customers have made specific allegations about compliance with the BPCPA."
'Demonstrably false or misleading'

Telus offered to manually search 200 customer files and provide records responding to the request, but said even that effort would "require multiple employees to be fully dedicated to the review for several weeks."

McColl's final report to the director of Consumer Protection B.C. claimed the lawyer's email directly contradicted the company's "earlier categorical representations that no such responsive records existed."

items: Rogers, Bell, Telus under fire for charging fees that 'appear' to violate new rules
Hundreds march in Vancouver to oppose planned AI data centres
Regulator launches inquiry into contentious fees charged by Rogers, Bell and Telus

blocks.text: "If potentially thousands of consumer files may contain potentially responsive material, then [Telus's] absolute statements of non-existence are inconsistent with any reasonable or diligent search," the report says.

"Difficulty retrieving records is not the same as the absence of records. By repeatedly stating that its searches revealed zero responsive items and asserting that no such records existed, [Telus] supplied information that was demonstrably false or misleading."
Consumer Protection B.C. issued a decision in June finding Telus had supplied misleading information and had failed to produce records.
The ruling came with a demand for $19,000 in fines and $22,000 to cover the costs of McColl's inspection.
The company was also ordered to "develop, revise and implement written policies and procedures governing its response to inspection orders and inquiries" from the regulator.

The fines and order for compliance are in limbo pending the outcome of the Supreme Court challenge in which Telus accuses Consumer Protection B.C. of making unlawful and unreasonably broad demands for information.In a statement, Telus said the company "fundamentally disagrees with the findings of Consumer Protection B.C., and we look forward to presenting our arguments in court."
Consumer Protection B.C. told CBC News the agency would not comment while the case is before the courts.

articles.title: Students return to Saskatoon high school missing 26 classrooms after fire
articles.summary: Students at Bethlehem Catholic High School will be back in class Wednesday for the first time since a fire last month — and the school day has been cut by half for most.

image.caption: Drone images taken last month of Bethlehem Catholic High School in Saskatoon show the main building and the burned-out remains of portables. The fire is believed to be suspicious. (Albert Couillard/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Saskatoon
Students at Bethlehem Catholic High School will be back in class Wednesday for the first time since a fire last month — and the school day has been cut by half for most.
Split-day schedule begins as arson investigation continues
Twenty-six portable classrooms were destroyed in the blaze at the Saskatoon school on Aug. 7. The fire has displaced nearly 800 students, including Kyson Kenny, who is entering Grade 11.

"It was crazy. I was up north and I was on my phone, and I kept looking at a bunch of videos my friend sent me — flames, giant flames everywhere. It was insane. Personally, I couldn't even believe it, actually," he said in an interview with CBC News.
Kenny said he visited the school last week to look at the football field, and it was covered in ashes.
"Bewildering," he said. "You usually see it in, like, media or TV shows, movies, but you never expected it to actually happen to you."
Police have said the origin of the fire is considered suspicious and an arson investigation is underway. No charges have been laid as of Tuesday afternoon.
How will it work?
Grades 9 and 10 have periods of instruction in the morning, and grades 11 and 12 take over the classrooms in the afternoon.

The other half of each student's day is set aside for tutorials, which are not mandatory for all students. The division is using some areas in the Shaw Centre next door, including a small gym, a multi-purpose room and meeting spaces.
Some students said the shortened classes will push youths away and result in more school work being done at home.
"There's probably going to be more homework for the first semester and stuff. And I don't know, it kind of sucks," said Cole Wagner, 16, a Grade 11 student on the football team.

items: Education Minister Everett Hindley will be on Blue Sky, CBC Sask.'s call-in show, from 12-1 p.m CST. Do you have a question for the minister? Email it to bluesky@cbc.ca, or call 1-800-716-2221 during the noon hour.

blocks.text: Kenny said he likes the shorter days but is worried about some of his classmates.
"There's a lot of people that like to skip classes, go out to malls," he said.
"Since it's not mandatory, I think it might not be the best for the students," he said of the tutorials.
Students head back to a Saskatoon school missing 26 classrooms

Tom Hickey, the superintendent of Greater Saskatoon Catholic Schools, said the situation has been hard for both students and teachers. Some staff were escorted by firefighters to collect their belongings after the blaze.
"That, for sure, was an emotional experience for some of our staff," he said. "You don't think about those things until a situation like this."
No timeline for rebuilding

The school does not yet know when the classrooms will be replaced. Hickey said those decisions involve structural engineers, insurers and the school division, and he expects more clarity within a couple of weeks.

He also said the decision to expand a school with portables rather than a permanent build rests with Saskatchewan's Ministry of Education, which maintains a priority list for major construction projects.

items: Students will return to class at Saskatoon school damaged by fire, school board says
Saskatoon high school fire considered 'suspicious,' police say

blocks.text: Until more space opens up, the split days will continue — potentially for the full semester.

"We've got to be prepared for anything," Hickey said. "If we have enough classrooms become available to us, really at any time in the year, we have the capability of switching back to a regular schedule."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Aishwarya Dudha is a reporter for CBC Saskatchewan based in Saskatoon. She specializes in immigration, justice and cultural issues and elevating voices of vulnerable people. She has previously worked for CBC News Network and Global News. You can email her at aishwarya.dudha@cbc.ca

articles.title: Tolosa turns up the heat in the courtroom, sparks hot exchanges
articles.summary: The public saw another side of Jay Tolosa in his impeachment court debut. It was a departure from his usual soft-spoken self in media interviews as spokesman of the prosecution.

blocks.text: FOR THE PROSECUTION. House prosecution panel legal spokesperson Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr., answers a question from the media during a press conference on June 22, 2026.
Angie de Silva/Rappler
The public saw another side of Jay Tolosa in his impeachment court debut. It was a departure from his usual soft-spoken self in media interviews as spokesman of the prosecution.
Lawyer Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr. is known by House reporters as the soft-spoken, mild-mannered legal spokesperson of the prosecution panel.

So it was a rather surprising turn to see the seasoned lawyer raise his voice, confront the witness, and argue with the defense team — and sometimes even with the presiding officer — on the 21st day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial.
Did he come in too hot?
Wednesday’s trial proceeding was not an ordinary day, and even the defense team knew it.
With the prosecution scheduled to call defense lawyer Michael Poa to the stand as a hostile witness, the defense team brought out its lead lawyer Sheila Sison to counter Tolosa’s line of questioning.

Tolosa came in with guns blazing, calling Poa an “abogadong walang alam (lawyer who does not know anything).” Sison took offense at Tolosa’s offer of testimony, and asked him to use a more professional language such as a “witness with no knowledge.” (But… isn’t that just almost the English equivalent of what Tolosa said?)
Escudero sided with Sison and agreed to strike the comments from the records, although it was only the first of many clashes between the two lawyers that day.

blocks.caption: Tolosa turns up the heat in the courtroom, sparks hot exchanges

blocks.text: Later, Tolosa tried to offer stipulations on Poa’s competence to expedite the proceedings, which Sison found unnecessary. Escudero said he found the stipulations irrelevant and asked Tolosa to move on “instead of going through these intramurals.”
Sison also challenged the prosecution’s effort to “read third-party statements” of Poa, and objected to Tolosa’s line of questioning on the basis of non-sequitur.

“This is not an opportunity that should be used by defense to pontificate, argue their position. That’s too much already. Under the rules, if you’re objecting to my question, just state the objection, no need to pontificate your theory of the case,” Tolosa remarked.
“The prosecution has had its fair share of pontificating, I think you are still ahead,” Escudero replied.

Pro-impeachment advocates who are rooting for the prosecution may have been disoriented by Tolosa’s litigation style, which is a stark contrast to how previous prosecutors — lawmakers Jinky Luistro and Joel Chua, as well as private prosecutors Mae Divinagracia, Lorna Kapunan, and Virgil Ligutan — handled past witnesses.

“No two lawyers are alike. Each has its own style. At the end of the day, the question is: did he deliver?” Ligutan said. “It is understandable that Attorney Tolosa’s style (would result) in a heated, tension-filled session.”
“One lawyer can bring tension, what more if two? And take note, the witness is also a lawyer…and a hostile witness,” Ligutan added. “It’s the perfect recipe for tension.”

blocks.caption: Tolosa turns up the heat in the courtroom, sparks hot exchanges

blocks.text: Tolosa had the most dead airs out of all lawyers who have appeared before the court so far (it took him a moment to sort his notes numerous times), and seemed to have the tendency to not move on quickly (he asked Escudero to “reconsider” a ruling he had made, prompting the presiding officer to say there’s no such thing).

But the prosecution’s spokesman also seemed to have found his footing after lunch, and was even able to extract from Poa a confirmation that he prepared DepEd’s defense before the Commission on Audit on the department’s confidential spending despite being unaware that there was a security officer who handled the secret funds.

Tolosa has an impressive portfolio: he lawyered for American soldier Joseph Pemberton, who was convicted of homicide in the killing of Filipino transgender woman Jennifer Laude. His other clients include some of the country’s biggest mining companies, flag carrier Philippine Airlines, and the local affiliate of Fortune 500 company Philip Morris International.
His legal background indicates this is not the first time he participated in — or maybe even caused — a heated courtroom proceeding.
“It’s nothing personal. We’re just doing our jobs,” Tolosa said after Wednesday’s trial. – Rappler.com

items: The Senate impeachment court is looking iton adjusting the trial schedule for Vice President Sara Duterte to prioritize deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.
Whole day trials are planned from October 1 to 2, 5 to 9, and 12 to 15, with a suspension from October 16 to November 8 for budget hearings, resuming on November 9 and 16.

MANILA,Philippines – The Senate impeachment court is eyeing adjustments to the calendar of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte to give the upper chamber time to focus on deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.

Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero announced on Wednesday, September 2, that the court is looking into holding “whole day” trials from October 1 to 2, 5 to 9, and 12 to 15, beginning at 10 am until early evening, to expedite the proceedings. There will be no plenary sessions on these dates.
The trial will then be suspended from October 16 to November 8 to give way to the Senate finance committee’s hearings on the proposed budgets of government agencies.
The impeachment trial will resume on November 9, then on November 16 — both Mondays — when the Senate is expected to endorse and tackle the proposed national budget at the plenary.
The regular trial schedule will resume on November 23 until the case is finished, under the eyed schedule.
Escudero said the proposed schedule will still be finetuned and finalized by next week.

blocks.caption: Senate impeachment court eyes adjustments in Sara Duterte trial schedule

blocks.text: “Sana maunawaan ninyo na kinakailangan namin bigyan ng panahon ang pinakaimportanteng panukalang batas na data naming aprubahan kada taon. Pero tinitiyak ko sa inyo na uukulan namin nang sapat at karampatang panahon ang impeachment para sa gayon ay matapos natin nang di kailangan patagalin nang mas matagal pa nang mas kinakailangan,” Escudero said, adding the proposed schedule remains subject to discussion and is expected to be finalized next week.

(We’re hoping the public will understand that we need time to finish the most important legislation we need to approve every year. But let me assure you that we will also give enough time for the trial so that we can finish it without letting it drag on longer than necessary.)

Escudero also said that compared to the Senate which has only 24 members, the House of Representatives has over 300 members who can focus on the budget deliberations and legislation while the House prosecution team is at the impeachment trial.

Senator-judge JV Ejercito, chair of the Senate committee on finance, underscored the importance of expediting the trial while alllotting time for budget deliberations. Its “either we finish the impeachment or have a reenacted budget,” he said.

Senator-judge Migz Zubiri noted that budget deliberations are whole-day affairs over a three-week period. He added that on top of the impeachment trial and the budget deliberations, the senators have to attend to priority legislation as well.

During the Wednesday trial, the impeachment court issued a new subpoena to former Department of Education special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda, who was previously excused from testifying to allow him to complete his two-week medical leave after suffering a stroke.

The prosecution expressed concern about Fajarda’s medical condition and raised the possibility of entering into a stipulation and excusing him from testifying as a witness. Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison asked the prosecutors to file the request in writing.
Escudero, for his part, said Fajarda may again be excused on Monday, September 7, if he would still be unfit to testify. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ‘He was always a bit of a groundbreaker’: David Bowie enters a new dimension in ‘extended reality’ documentary
articles.summary:
Hundreds of unseen images of the star feature at the Venice film festival, alongside virtual worlds exploring wildfires, wolves and the birth of stars

David Bowie shares the bill with…

blocks.text: David Bowie shares the bill with starmen, firefighters and Walt Disney wolves at the 10th anniversary edition of Venice Immersive, the film festival’s pioneering showcase for new forms of storytelling. David Bowie: Unseen Unheard – a 3D documentary featuring hundreds of previously unseen images – is among 69 XR (extended reality) pieces playing at the event’s regular base on Lazzaretto Vecchio, a repurposed small island off the Venice Lido.

Venice Immersive’s 10th birthday marks a milestone for an event which aims to provide a bridge between emergent technology and traditional narrative cinema. But the programme’s organisers are at pains to emphasise the ongoing scope of a project that has in recent years prompted similar sections at the Cannes, Geneva and Toronto film festivals. “This is not a retrospective,” declares the official festival blurb that welcomes guests to the island. It almost sounds like a warning.

“This is such a fast-evolving medium,” says Liz Rosenthal, Venice Immersive’s co-curator. “We’re basically witnessing new forms of art being crafted in real time. So we’re already looking forward to the next 10 years. I think we’re very much at a turning point in terms of the platforms and technology that’s available – and this in turn will shape the nature of the storytelling itself.”

blocks.caption: Sound and vision … David Bowie on stage at the Serious Moonlight tour in 1983, a scene from David Bowie: Unseen Unheard.  Photograph: Denis O’Regan

blocks.text: Billed as an immersive spatial-sound documentary, David Bowie: Unseen Unheard is a personal portrait of the singer by Denis O’Regan, who worked as Bowie’s official photographer. The installation plays out across eight screens and 84 hidden speakers, folding 12 Bowie songs alongside O’Regan’s commentary and archive of nearly 800 photographs. Bowie died in 2016, but the project was conceived and developed with the full support and cooperation of the late singer’s estate.

“David would have loved this, definitely,” O’Regan says. “And he would have loved it going into the Venice film festival. He was always a bit of a groundbreaker. David loved his technology. He loved making things happen and experimenting with new ideas, like his Bowie bonds or Bowie.net. Listen to the Aladdin Sane album from 1973 and he’s already writing lyrics like, ‘Pour me out another phone, I’ll ring and see if your friends are home’. The thing about David is that he wasn’t just about the music. He was about mime, visuals, theatre, film.” It is this hybrid quality, O’Regan adds, that makes him a natural fit for Venice Immersive.

Fittingly, David Bowie: Unseen Unheard rubs shoulders with a rogues’ gallery of genre-defying new work from around the globe. The climate crisis is a major focus at this year’s edition, with Felix Gaedtke and Gayatri Parameswaran’s Solomon Islands-set Solwata, Barthélemy Antoine-Loeff and Hugo Arcier’s interactive The White Saboteur and the LA wildfire documentary Out of the Ashes all tackling the issue of human-made climate change.

Other potential highlights include the immersive nature documentaries Galápagos: The Last Eden and Disneynature’s Wolf, which conducts a virtual tour of Canada’s remote Ellesmere Island. James Elliott Mizroch’s VR installation Smithsonian Starstruck goes further still, inviting users to step inside the cosmos to watch a star being born.

“The first years of Venice Immersive were more about experimentation,” says Rosenthal. “The pieces were either playing with the various formats or they were these small side projects of big media properties. Now we’re seeing big works that have a proper distribution strategy. That means that the work has a life that extends far beyond the island. They can be seen and enjoyed by people around the world.”

articles.title: Senate court orders COA employee, 2 others to testify in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday ordered Commission on Audit (COA) employee Bresilio Sabaldan and two others to testify in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from September…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 6:35pm

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday ordered Commission on Audit (COA) employee Bresilio Sabaldan and two others to testify in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from September 7 to 9.
In his order, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said the court had granted the subpoena request filed by lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas.
The subpoena also covers former Department of Education (DepEd) Assistant Secretary Sunshine Cherry Fajarda and Police Major Jovelyn Magay.

Luistro said the prosecution intends to present Sabaldan, Fajarda and Magay as witnesses next week, along with Fajarda’s husband, former DepEd special disbursing officer Eduard Fajarda, and Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) official Marizza Grande.

Luistro also said Magay and Sabaldan were among the reserve witnesses identified by the prosecution in its pretrial brief, or court submission listing its witnesses and the purpose of their testimonies.

Luistro, however, said the prosecution may decide not to present Eduard Fajarda as a witness if the defense agrees to certain stipulations regarding his role in the disbursement of DepEd’s confidential funds.
Escudero said the prosecution should submit the proposed stipulations in writing for the defense team’s review.

The prosecution is currently presenting its evidence on Article 1 of the impeachment complaint, which alleges that Duterte committed an impeachable offense through the misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of P612.5 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and DepEd when she was still education secretary.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Poa: COA yet to reverse clearance of DepEd's P75-M confi fund spending in 2023
articles.summary: Defense counsel and former undersecretary Michael Poa said Wednesday the Commission on Audit (COA) has yet to reverse its decision clearing the Department of Education's (DepEd) P75-million…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 6:34pm

Defense counsel and former undersecretary Michael Poa said Wednesday the Commission on Audit (COA) has yet to reverse its decision clearing the Department of Education's (DepEd) P75-million confidential fund spending for the first two quarters of 2023.

Poa made the testimony during the cross examination of lead defense counsel Sheila Sison on Day 21 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, who served at the helm of the DepEd when the confidential funds in question were disbursed.
Sison asked Poa if he was aware of efforts or moves from COA to reconsider the credit notice or clearance on DepEd's P75-million confidential fund spending in 2023.
Poa replied: "As far as I'm aware, none at the moment."
Likewise, Poa also testified that COA did not issue a notice of suspension and notice of disallowance on DepEd's confidential funds spending from first to third quarter.

During the re-cross examination of private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr., Poa was asked if the credit notice issued by the COA on the P75 million changes the testimony of two military officials that the certifications that the DepEd used to liquidate P15 million out of the P75 million confidential fund spending does cover the DepEd’s confidential fund spending.

Tolosa was referring to earlier testimonies of Army Colonels Maranos Boransing II and Magtanggol Panopio on Tuesday before the Senate impeachment court, who said that their certifications requested them by then-DepEd undersecretary Nolasco Mempin were merely for attendance and conduct of seminars for the youth.
"All of these matters are not changed just because a credit notice was issued, correct, sir?" Tolosa asked.
Poa replied, "Correct." — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Fatal Sydney shooting could be another case of mistaken identity, police say
articles.summary:
A man shot dead in Merrylands West was not known to police, in a case with similarities to Monday’s killing in Campbelltown

  • Get our

blocks.text: New South Wales police are investigating the shooting death of a man in Sydney’s west as a potential case of mistaken identity, marking the second fatal shooting incident in as many days.
Emergency services responded to reports of a shooting at a home in Merrylands West at about 3.15pm on Wednesday, where a man believed to be in his 30s sustained a gunshot wound.
The victim, who was yet to be formally identified, was treated by paramedics but died at the scene.
Police said the property was a location known to police for organised crime, but said “the victim has no links that we’re aware of to organised crime”.
At a press conference, Supt Simon Glasser said it was unclear what the man who was shot was doing at the location or his connection to the residents.
“The person who we believe has been shot has no adverse holdings with police. People that are linked to this address are known to Sydney to organised crime,” he said.
“It’s very early on in the investigation, however, there is a possibility that the wrong person has been shot by those offenders.”
The alleged shooting marks the second incident of its kind this week.

On Tuesday, 23-year-old Marco Tapia was shot dead in his bed as his family slept at about 3.40am after multiple attackers were believed to have forced their way into a two-storey home in Glen Alpine, near Campbelltown, in south-west Sydney.
That case was being investigated as a case of mistaken identity, police said, because Tapia was not known to authorities and had nothing more than a traffic offence on his record.
His martial arts gym remembered him in a public tribute overnight.
“We lost a real one today,” they wrote, adding: “Rest easy Marco, one of us forever.”

The Alameddine network, a notorious crime family, and the Coconut Cartel, an emerging crime-for-hire network, have allegedly become embroiled in a feud, spilling into shootings across Sydney in recent months.
after newsletter promotion
Acting Supt Gretchen Atkins of Campbelltown police said on Tuesday she was aware of online posts about the Glen Alpine case and said everything was under consideration.
The NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, said the incidents showed gangland violence was out of control.
“We need to be very clear about the threat on our streets and that is dangerous organised criminals … innocent people have been in the firing line way too often,” she said.

“Whether it is a young man, a student sleeping in his bed at night [or] a grandfather who’s kidnapped and murdered,” referring to the Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian, who was taken from his home on 13 February and later found dead.
She suggested the government was not doing enough to stop the shootings.

But the police minister, Yasmin Catley, criticised Sloane, whose electorate is in Sydney’s eastern suburbs, over her position on the state’s gun buyback scheme, launched after December’s Bondi massacre.
“The member for Vaucluse, we must remember, is also the same person that wants to squash [national gun buyback reform],” Catley said.
“She wants more guns on the street and wants to blame the police for not doing their job … I’m not tolerating that, I won’t have a bar of that.”
