articles.title: Four charged with murder after newborn baby stabbed to death in Sheffield
articles.summary:
The two men and two women are also accused of causing or allowing death of a child and perverting course of justice

Four people have been charged with murder after a newborn baby girl was…

blocks.text: Four people have been charged with murder after a newborn baby girl was stabbed to death in Sheffield.

Two men and two women are to appear in court on Wednesday accused of murder, causing or allowing the death of a child, and perverting the course of justice by taking steps to conceal the killing of an infant.
A 15-year-old girl, who cannot be named for legal reasons due to her age, has been charged with perverting the course of justice.
Police were called to the Wincobank area of Sheffield on Sunday morning after reports of concern for the safety of an infant.
Officers searched a property on Holywell Heights and found the baby.
A forensic postmortem examination identified the baby’s cause of death as resulting from stab wounds.
Police said Andrea Skopova, 20, Peter Horvath, 19, Peter Horvath, 38, and Nina Horvathova, 37, were charged with murder on Tuesday evening.
The five defendants are in custody and will appear at Sheffield magistrates court on Wednesday. Two women, aged 26 and 37, who were arrested on suspicion of murder remain on bail.

articles.title: DepEd ex-disbursing exec Fajarda may no longer be presented as witness
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Lead House prosecutor Gerville Luistro said they may no longer present the testimony of former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda before…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Lead House prosecutor Gerville Luistro said they may no longer present the testimony of former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda before the Senate impeachment court due to his poor health.
However, Luistro noted on Wednesday that this will only happen should the defense team agree to its request for stipulations.
Stipulations refer to an agreement formed by opposing parties in a legal proceeding to accept certain facts as true without needing to prove them.

“It is our intention not to aggravate his condition. As a matter of fact, it is likewise our intention to excuse him, if possible, from the rigors of being presented in the witnesses’ stand,” said Luistro in a manifestation.
“However, that is without sacrificing the case of the prosecution, and that is why we would like to explore the possibility of entering into stipulations,” she told the impeachment court.
“And if the defense will agree, then there is a possibility as well that the prosecution will move to dispense with the testimony of Edward Fajarda,” she offered.
Court presiding officer and Senator-judge Francis “Chiz” Escudero, for his part, directed the prosecution to submit its request for stipulations to the defense team in writing.
He also stated that the court is ready to excuse Fajarda on Monday, Sept. 7 should he be not healthy enough to answer the subpoena issued to him.
Escudero also said that the Senate’s own doctors will check if Fajarda is fit to attend trial.

“However, that does not preclude [the prosecution] from submitting a request for stipulation before the week is over, so we can get the comment of the counsel for the respondent on Monday,” said the presiding officer.
The presentation of Fajarda before the Senate impeachment court was moved to Sept. 7 from Aug. 25 after the court received a medical certificate informing them of Fajarda suffering a stroke. /apl

articles.title: Only P80M received so far from Leviste solar firm’s P24B fine – DOE
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The government has received only P80 million, so far, from the P24 billion penalty imposed on Batangas 1st Dist. Rep. Leandro Leviste’s solar energy company, according to the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The government has received only P80 million, so far, from the P24 billion penalty imposed on Batangas 1st Dist. Rep. Leandro Leviste’s solar energy company, according to the Department of Energy (DOE) on Wednesday.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin divulged this after Akbayan Partylist Rep. Chel Diokno raised the penalty issue during the House Committee on Appropriations’ budget hearing for the DOE on Wednesday.

The DOE recently imposed a P24 billion penalty against Leviste’s Solar Philippines Power Project Holdings Inc. (SPPHI) for supposedly failing to produce power it committed to deliver under more than 30 service contracts with the government.
“P80 million, Mr. Chair,” Garin said when asked by Diokno about the amount the government received from the solar firm’s penalty.

When pressed on how the DOE plans to compel SPPHI to return the total P24 billion to the government, Garin said a criminal complaint has already been filed with the Department of Justice (DOJ), and a civil case has been lodged with the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG).
“The issue currently is in the hands of the DOJ… and then the OSG is handling the civil case,” said Garin.
“The purpose of these cases is also to recover the P14 billion in expired bonds, is that correct?” Diokno further asked, in which Garin answered in the affirmative.
Why not blacklist Solar PH?
During the interpellation, Diokno also pressed whether the DOE has taken any steps to blacklist SPPHI.

Garin explained that since blacklisting or even suspension of companies was not included in the DOE’s circular, the agency recently issued guidelines regarding the blacklisting, pointing out that “we’re working on it.”
“I think a month or two months ago, we issued a new circular on GenCos’ (generation companies) accountability, which gives them three strikes, and we can blacklist them,” Garin said.
Diokno then requested the guidelines and pointed out that the solar firm must already be blacklisted, which the DOE vowed to comply with.
Leviste recently denied that SPPPHI failed to meet its targets, pointing out that projects were not actually granted permits to proceed. /gsg

articles.title: Strict segregation, proper landfill design to fix waste problem – DENR
articles.summary: MANILA – The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has urged local government units (LGUs) to strengthen waste segregation and landfill management, citing Bayawan City’s consistent…

blocks.text: MANILA – The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has urged local government units (LGUs) to strengthen waste segregation and landfill management, citing Bayawan City’s consistent and proper waste management.

In a news release Wednesday, the DENR cited Bayawan City in Negros Oriental as an example of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s vision for LGUs to become “laboratories of workable solutions and showcases of best practices.”

“Proper landfill design is possible, and all LGUs should follow the example of Bayawan,” Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said during a recent visit to the Bayawan City Waste Management and Ecology Center (BCWMEC).
He commended the city for its effective solid waste management practices under Republic Act 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000).
Cuna also urged other LGUs to replicate Bayawan City’s operational framework.
“President Bongbong Marcos has called on our barangays and LGUs to become laboratories of workable solutions and showcases of best practices,” he said.

“Bayawan is a clear example of that vision in action. Through strong local leadership, community participation, and collaboration with the DENR, the city has shown that proper solid waste management can be sustained and can build cleaner, healthier communities,” he added.
Bayawan City used to be filled with unsegregated garbage, including plastic waste, and open dumping that even reached remote areas.

The 27.4-hectare Bayawan City Waste Management and Ecology Center (BCWMEC) in Sitio Omod, Barangay Maninihon now includes a sanitary landfill cell, Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), composting unit, special waste vault, and septage management system, serving 28 barangays, covering about 117,900 residents, including five neighboring LGUs and three private firms.
Local officials noted that it took years to develop the current system.
In the late 1990s, household waste was being dumped in Sitio Buli-Buli, Barangay Banga, creating health and environmental risks.
With the DENR’s guidance, the city adopted a Solid Waste Management Plan in 2002 that required segregation at source, systematic collection, recycling, and composting.
However, in 2023, Bayawan faced compliance problems and even received a Notice of Violation (NOV) from the DENR after its effluent wastewater failed to meet required standards.

“There was a time na hindi pumasa yung effluent wastewater naming (when our effluent wastewater did not pass), and DENR issued us a Notice of Violation,” BCWMEC Assistant Manager Irvin Joshua Elum said.

“But they did not stop there. Tinulungan nila kami kung pano ma-resolve yung situation, nagbigay sila ng technical advice and thankfully, na-address yung problem, and nakapasa na tayo (They helped us figure out how to resolve the situation, giving us technical advice, and thankfully, the problem was addressed, and we passed),” he added.
Bayawan also introduced a Pay-As-You-Throw scheme requiring designated stickers on sacks of residual waste before collection, refusing unsegregated waste, and penalizing violators.
Along with strict enforcement of waste segregation, the city launched a massive information campaign and deployed deputized enforcers to monitor illegal dumping and nighttime violations.
As a result, about 80 percent of waste is now segregated before final disposal, allowing recyclables to be recovered and reducing the volume of waste reaching the landfill.

The city has since received recognition for its waste management initiatives, including awards from DENR-Negros Island Region and the Presidential Lingkod Bayan Award given by the Civil Service Commission to the Bayawan Integrated Waste Management Team.
Cuna said the bigger lesson is that LGUs need to consistently enforce waste management laws while involving residents in the process.

“Bayawan shows us that environmental laws work when they are implemented consistently and when communities are made part of the solution. This is a model that other LGUs can learn from and adapt to their own local conditions,” he said.

articles.title: Mindanao grid placed under red, yellow alerts
articles.summary: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) placed the Mindanao grid under red and yellow alerts several times on Wednesday due to insufficient power supply and…

blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) placed the Mindanao grid under red and yellow alerts several times on Wednesday due to insufficient power supply and high consumer demand.A red alert was raised over the grid from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. and from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m, indicating that power supply was insufficient to meet consumer demand and the transmission grid’s regulating requirements.Meanwhile, yellow alerts were declared from 12:00 p.m. to 1:00 p.m., 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m., and 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., signaling an operating margin that is insufficient to meet contingency requirements.

The extension of the alert declarations was driven by the unavailability of Mindanao’s large coal plants—specifically Units 1 and 2 of the GNPower Kauswagan (GNPK) coal-fired power plant in Lanao del Norte, and Unit 2 of the Therma South, Inc. (TSI) coal-fired power plant located in the boundary of Davao City and Sta. Cruz, Davao del Sur—alongside a significant increase in the region’s demand forecast and a decrease in overall available generation.Authorities noted that a total of 855.1 megawatts is currently unavailable to the grid, with multiple plants on forced outage spanning back to previous months, while seven plants are running at derated capacity./coa

articles.title: Fire displaces 19 families in Iloilo City
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — Nineteen families, or 83 individuals, were affected by an hour-long fire that hit a residential area in Veterans Village in this city late Tuesday night. The Iloilo City Emergency…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — Nineteen families, or 83 individuals, were affected by an hour-long fire that hit a residential area in Veterans Village in this city late Tuesday night.

The Iloilo City Emergency Operations Center (EOC), in its first situation report issued at 9 a.m. Wednesday, said 12 houses were affected by the blaze, five of which were totally damaged while seven were partially damaged.
The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) said there were no casualties.
The fire broke out at around 10:05 p.m. in Veterans Village, City Proper. Firefighters declared the blaze under control at 10:45 p.m. and declared it out at 11:03 p.m.
The cause of the fire remained under investigation as of Wednesday.
Personnel from the BFP-Iloilo City Fire Station, Iloilo City Police Office, ICAG and Federation Iloilo Volunteer Fire Brigade, along with other volunteer groups, responded to the incident.
The affected families were brought to a day care center identified by the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) as an evacuation site.
The CSWDO assessed the affected residents and damaged houses and distributed food and non-food assistance.

Relief assistance included rice, canned goods, drinking water, hygiene kits, sleeping kits, and water containers. The affected families were provided a hygiene kit, sleeping kit, and jerry can, the EOC report said.
The BFP continued mapping and investigating the fire site to determine the cause of the blaze.

Meanwhile, the Iloilo City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office coordinated with barangay officials and the CSWDO and disseminated updates to the city’s disaster response clusters and the public.

A separate local report early Wednesday initially placed the number of affected houses at 10, four of which were destroyed. The subsequent EOC situation report placed the official initial count at 12 houses, 19 families, and 83 individuals as of 9 a.m. /coa

articles.summary: The impeachment court on Wednesday, September 2, heard from its latest hostile witness, defense counsel and former DepEd spokesperson and chief of staff Michael Poa.

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 5:30pm
MANILA, Philippines — The impeachment court on Wednesday, September 2, heard from its latest hostile witness, defense counsel and former DepEd spokesperson and chief of staff Michael Poa.
Poa, who is also part of Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team, was DepEd's chief of staff and later concurrently officer-in-charge undersecretary for finance under then-Secretary Duterte.
He signed the department's official reply to a Commission on Audit inquiry into the department's P112.5 million in confidential funds.

Prosecution offered him as a witness specifically because, in counsel to the prosecution Benjamin Tolosa Jr.'s words, Poa was made to answer for the use and liquidation of those funds "despite knowing nothing" about how it was actually spent on the ground, and because, in the prosecution's view, "every road leads to the vice president."

Duterte's trial entered its 21st day today with hours of testimony chipping at DepEd's paper trail justifying P15.54 million in confidential fund rewards, repeated procedural clashes between prosecution and defense over how far Tolosa could go in confronting Poa with his own past testimonies at the House of Representatives, and a new stretch of trial dates set for October and November.
Here are the highlights from today's proceedings:
1. Poa didn't know DepEd had a security officer until House hearings

Poa testified he was not aware DepEd had a designated security officer handling confidential funds, Col. Dennis Nolasco, until it surfaced in House hearings, well after he had already signed off on DepEd's response to COA.

Under questioning from Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, Poa said the special disbursing officer he consulted while preparing that response, DepEd SDO Edward Fajarda, never told him he personally handed rewards to informants.

Whenever he asked for details, Poa said the officer pointed only to "the field." Poa confirmed he never spoke with Nolasco and didn't know he existed at the time: "Hindi ko po alam na may security officer at hindi ko po nakita or nakilala si Colonel Nolasco nung panahon ko po sa DepEd."
Asked why he didn't approach the security officer directly, Poa said he would have, had he known one existed.

Sen. Risa Hontiveros pressed further on when and how Poa learned this. Poa said he only found out during the 2024 House hearings, realizing then that "the field" the SDO kept referring to was actually Nolasco.

Hontiveros' expressed disbelief, saying: "Para katulad 'yun ng hindi alam ng chief of staff ko sa office ko dito sa Senado na may chief security ako at hindi kilala ng chief of staff ko 'yung chief security. Impossible para sa akin."

Poa agreed it struck him as unusual too, but added that by the time he learned of Nolasco's role, impeachment complaints against Duterte were already being filed and he had become her legal counsel, limiting what he can now discuss under attorney-client privilege.
Meanwhile, Sen. Imee Marcos pressed Poa on how, as DepEd chief of staff, he could have had no role in confidential funds at all.
Throughout the direct and cross examination, Poa repeatedly testified to having no personal knowledge of operations on the ground.

Poa described Duterte's office as "highly compartmentalized" where different units would be confined to knowing only what was within their mandate. Poa said Duterte instructed him to primarily keep DepEd's undersecretaries from feuding, and achieving the targets under DepEd's "Matatag" agenda, the post-pandemic education reform DepEd launched under Duterte.

Asked by Hontiveros whether OVP and DepEd staff who assisted Duterte could face legal liability if she's convicted, and whether he himself could be included, Poa answered: "Possible naman po... Posible po. Sana po hindi, pero posible po."
2. Prosecution, defense clash repeatedly over video playback and past testimony

Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison objected repeatedly as Tolosa tried to confront Poa with his October 2024 House testimonies, at several points successfully blocking playback of video clips of Poa's exchanges with House members.

At one point, Tolosa hit back at the objections, saying: "This is not an opportunity that should be used by the Defense to pontificate [or] argue their position... Just state your objection, no need to pontificate and explain your theory of the case."
At this, presiding officer Sen. Chiz Escudero has quipped: "The prosecution has had its fair share of pontificating. I think you're still ahead by a couple."

He ultimately sided with the defense on the issue, limiting Tolosa to reading Poa's own prior answers into the record rather than replaying footage, after Sison argued that showing a lawmaker's side of the exchange amounted to using a third party's statements against the witness.
Earlier in the day, Escudero also ordered a remark by Tolosa describing Poa as "abugadong walang alam," a lawyer who knows nothing, stricken from the record for being discourteous.
Tolosa had explained his use of the phrase was in the context of Poa claiming no personal knowledge of how confidential funds were spent during actual activities.
3. New witnesses, and a packed trial calendar through November
Before adjourning, the court issued subpoenas for five more witnesses to testify September 7 to 9: Fajarda himself, Philippine Statistics Authority official Marizza Grande, and three others.
The prosecution also floated a number of possible stipulations to spare Fajardo, reportedly in poor health, from testifying in person.
Escudero also outlined a tentative schedule of full-day sessions running October 1–2 and October 5–9, pausing for the Senate's budget hearings, then resuming for two Mondays only in November.

Senators JV Ejercito and Juan Miguel Zubiri warned of the strain of running the trial alongside plenary sessions and the 2027 national budget deliberations. Ejercito said the Senate risks passing a reenacted budget without adjustments to its schedule. A caucus has been set where senators will discuss their options.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau voters approve new constitution expanding presidential powers
articles.summary:
Changes include fewer seats in parliament and new rules on presidential candidates ahead of December elections

Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution significantly expanding…

blocks.text: Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution significantly expanding presidential powers ahead of elections due in December.

According to provisional results, 70% of voters approved sweeping changes in the tiny west African state’s first constitutional amendment since revisions that ended the one-party socialist state more than three decades ago.
The turnout for Sunday’s referendum was reportedly over 55%, amounting to an estimated 544,060 people.

The new constitution will reduce the number of seats in parliament from 102 to 65 and cut electoral constituencies from 29 to 12. New provisions will require presidential candidates to have lived continuously in the country for at least five years before the vote, which is believed to target diaspora-based politicians with significant followings.

The referendum’s outcome is expected to pave the way for December’s elections, which many hope will steady the political landscape in Guinea-Bissau, which has been through a series of politically turbulent periods since its declaration of independence from Portugal was globally recognised in 1974. Since then it has had at least 10 coup attempts, half of which have been successful.

The most recent came after last November’s disputed presidential elections. Both candidates declared themselves winners, citing electoral malpractice by the other’s camp. The military forcefully intervened, setting up a transitional ruling council headed by Gen Horta Inta-A Na Man, a former military chief of general staff.
Na Man said: “What we want after this referendum is to allow whoever wins the elections to see out their mandate without hindrance.”
Nelson Moreira, the second vice-president of the transitional council, said the outgoing constitution, which came into effect in 1993, had often been cited as “the cause of instability in Guinea”.

The leading opposition party, the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC), which was barred from fielding a presidential candidate in the 2025 election, had asked its supporters to boycott the referendum, which it called a democratic farce.
“What will happen on 30 August is the continuation of the coup d’état carried out on 26 November,” its leader, Domingos Simões Pereira, had said.

articles.title: Palace exec: Gov't not slow vs floods
articles.summary: Malacañang on Wednesday said the government was not slow when it came to flood control, as President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is only responding to decades of institutional neglect.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 5:15pm
Malacañang on Wednesday said the government was not slow when it came to flood control, as President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is only responding to decades of institutional neglect.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said Marcos could feel the people’s anger when it came to corruption in the government, especially in the flood control scam. He wanted the people to know that the government was active and responsive.

“Hindi po mabagal ang pamahalaan. Marami lang po talagang dapat na ayusin na sinasabi rin po ng mga eksperto na hindi inayos ng ilang dekada. Hindi isang dekada. Hindi dalawang dekada. Halos apat na dekadang naiwan kay Pangulo ang inaayos ngayon,” Castro said during a press briefing.

(The government is not slow. There is just a lot that needs to be fixed that even experts say have not been fixed in decades. Not one decade. Not two decades. But almost four decades of neglect has been left to the President that he is fixing now.)
Castro said Marcos is going through these projects one by one.
The Palace official emphasized that even on break days, the agencies were acting under Marcos’ orders. Marcos has told government agencies to be better prepared for the effects of climate change.
The Marcos administration is currently working to update the flood mitigation plans of 18 major river basins across the country.
As of May, the Department of Public Works and Highways already has 16 out of the 18 master plans and feasibility studies for the river basins. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: PH stunting rate among children under 2 drops to 21.1% in 2025 -- DOH
articles.summary: The stunting rate among children under 2 years old in the Philippines declined from 22.5% in 2023 to 21.1% in 2025, the Department of Health (DOH) reported Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 5:15pm
The stunting rate among children under 2 years old in the Philippines declined from 22.5% in 2023 to 21.1% in 2025, the Department of Health (DOH) reported Wednesday.

“Eight out of 10 children aged 2 years old and below have adequate height for their age. The stunting rate slightly decreased from 22.5% in 2023 to 21.1% in 2025,” DOH Secretary Edwin Mercado said during a House budget hearing.
“Although we are still far from our target, especially our Millennium Development targets,” he added.
The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) 2023–2028 aims to reduce the stunting rate among children under 5 years old to 17.9% or lower by 2028.
Stunting is a condition caused by chronic malnutrition, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life. It can impair brain development and cognitive function.

The DOH also reported that two in three children are fully immunized. Mercado said the agency is stepping up efforts to increase immunization coverage, which remains below its target of 95% of children being fully immunized.
Households with access to basic water supply stood at 82.7%, below the target of 94%.
Meanwhile, 64.5% of Filipino families have access to modern family planning methods, also below the target of 72.5%.
In April, the DOH reported that the country's HIV treatment cascade stood at 61% diagnosed, 66% on treatment, and 57% with a suppressed viral load, compared with the global 95-95-95 targets.

“We already have programs that will expand PhilHealth's Outpatient HIV/AIDS Treatment (OHAT) program to cover preparatory or pre-emptive HIV treatments. We will also expand testing to help raise coverage toward our target of 95%,” Mercado said.
The DOH also reported that 367,226 tuberculosis patients had completed their treatment, while 262,569 individuals had access to essential mental health medicines.
During the same hearing, the DOH said TB drugs and related commodities are expected to be delivered to the Philippines between late October and November. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Range Rover launches its first electric vehicle, with starting price of £154,070
articles.summary:
Fully electric SUV unveiled after year-long delay and will be built at Jaguar Land Rover’s plant in Solihull

Range Rover has launched its first electric vehicle – a year later than planned –…

blocks.text: Range Rover has launched its first electric vehicle – a year later than planned – offering a greener option for fans of gargantuan British-made SUVs who are also conscious about the climate crisis.
Due to be built in Solihull, the home of the marque since 1970, the vehicle comes with an eye-watering price tag, starting at £154,070.
However, the delayed launch marks a milestone departure from cars powered by fossil fuels for Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which is owned by India’s Tata Motors but headquartered in Coventry in the UK.

It also provides a much-needed moment of positivity for JLR, which reported falling profits earlier this year as it counted the cost of Donald Trump’s tariff wars and supply chain disruption after a crippling cyber-attack last year.
JLR said it had given extra training to 10,500 staff working on the project and that the car had undergone testing equivalent to 38 trips around the world, more than any other Range Rover.
The company said the luxury vehicle, which can reach 60mph in 4.3 seconds, heralded “a new era of enhanced refinement and capability”.

While the model’s electric powertrain will limit its impact on the environment compared with JLR’s petrol and diesel models, SUVs of its size are consistently linked to higher numbers of road deaths in accidents involving pedestrians.

However, Ranger Rover’s bespoke commissioning service does mean that buyers have an “extended choice of near limitless paint colours and finishes, elevated materials, tailored colour combinations and personalisation details including unique embroidery”.
Martin Limpert, the managing director of Range Rover, said the vehicle was the end product of a “decade of considered engineering and technological development”.
after newsletter promotion

Production at Solihull will be supported by the automaker’s propulsion manufacturing centre, in Wolverhampton, which makes battery packs and electric drive units, as well as traditional internal combustion engines.

articles.title: Impeach court eyes whole day October trials, focus on budget in November
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The Senate impeachment court is considering holding whole day proceedings for Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, cancelling plenary sessions starting October until…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Senate impeachment court is considering holding whole day proceedings for Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, cancelling plenary sessions starting October until the second regular session of the chamber resumes on November 9.

Presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero informed the court of the proposal “subject to finality” as the chamber struggles to set a schedule for trial and legislative work amid committee hearings for the 2027 national budget.

“On October 1 and 2 our trial shall be for the entire day, from morning until afternoon, we will have no session and even up to early evening. On October 5 to 9, also the whole day from 10 am until early evening… On October 12 to 15, Monday to Thursday, whole day as well until early evening,” Escudero suggested.
“We shall be suspending the trial to give way to the committee hearings of the [Senate] committee on finance… We have to await the approval of the House before break on October 8,” he added.
Escudero also said that there will only be two trial days for the first two weeks of November for budget deliberations.

“We will resume trial on November 9 and 16. Both a Monday. For the following two weeks when we resume on November 9, we will be deliberating on the budget on the floor which usually takes until the wee hours of November,” he said.
After budget deliberations, the trial will “proceed to normal programming on November 23 until we finish the case,” Escudero proposed.
In response, Senate Finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito hoped that a caucus could be held to find “the best solution” to accommodate all Senate matters.
Senator-judge Juan Miguel Zubiri also lamented that the impeachment trial takes away the chamber’s time to tackle legislative matters, adding that the 12-hour work days thus far have been exhausting.

“We really have to meet on how we can make our time work. We’re doing three things at the same time for 24 of us – for a small number of people… We just need to know how we can expedite this,” Zubiri said. /gsg

articles.title: Angara: Utilize new hazard assessment tool to manage class disruptions
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—The Department of Education (DepEd) told school administrators on Wednesday to use its new hazard assessment tool to prevent class disruptions caused by natural disasters. “We are…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The Department of Education (DepEd) told school administrators on Wednesday to use its new hazard assessment tool to prevent class disruptions caused by natural disasters.

“We are calling all school leaders, teachers and (Disaster Risk Reduction and Management) coordinators to use LIGTAS+ as part of our regular disaster preparedness,” said Education Secretary Sonny Angara in a statement on Wednesday.

Launched on Aug. 26, Project LIGTAS+, or the Learning Institution Geohazard Tracking and Assessment for Safety, is a decision-support platform that converts raw weather and geological data into school-level safety alerts.
Angara emphasized the need to shift from reactive disaster response, stating that the project would allow schools to gauge risks early and respond before disruptions worsen.
“Hindi pwedeng lagi na lang tayong nag-aabang kung kailan babagyo o lilindol bago tayo kumilos,” said Angara.
(“We can’t always just wait when a storm or earthquake will happen before we take action.”)

With LIGTAS+, we can anticipate risks early so our school leaders can make timely, informed decisions before hazards turn into emergencies,” Angara added, stating that disaster preparedness requires clear and reliable information.
The platform streamlined data across all DepEd administrative levels, enabling school heads, teachers, and disaster response coordinators to securely log in using their official credentials.
Its AI-powered interactive map identifies risks from storms, heat, and volcanic activity near more than 47,000 public schools nationwide.

It also collated weather, satellite and geographical data from key government scientific agencies the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration and the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology.
Climate data was also gathered fom international scientific agencies U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the European Union’s Copernicus satellite data collection.
However, DepEd clarified that the project only serves as a decision-support tool and is not meant to replace official advisories, established protocols, and field assessments.
Angara said that using these new technologies alongside their partner agencies would help schools prepare for disasters swiftly.

“Through LIGTAS+, we are giving our school leaders the right tools and information to act early, keep our learners safe, and ensure that learning continues even during disasters,” he said. —With report from Sheridan Delfino /mr

articles.title: Romualdez camp free to comment; admin adhering to due process – Palace
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Wednesday said the camp of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is free to voice out opinions but asserted that the administration follows due process and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Wednesday said the camp of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is free to voice out opinions but asserted that the administration follows due process and evidence.
These remarks came after the camp of presidential cousin alleged that the Office of the Ombudsman seems to have “prejudged” the official as the mastermind of the flood control scandal.

“Kung anuman po iyong naging statement ng kampo po ni dating Speaker Martin Romualdez, iyan po ay karapatan nila. At kung iyan ang kanilang nararamdaman ay hindi po natin mapipigilan,” said Palace press officer Claire Castro at a briefing when asked for a comment on the matter.
(Whatever the statement made by the camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez, that is their right. And if that is how they feel, we cannot stop them.)
Castro acknowledged that there are always two opposing sides: the complainant and the accused, and that it is just normal for Romualdez to defend himself.

“Kung malakas naman din po ang ebidensiya ng sinumang respondents ay kakayanin naman nila. Kung iniisip nila na sila’y tinututukan lamang at kaya naman nilang ipagtanggol ang kanilang mga sarili, nasa kanila na po iyan,” she said.
(If the evidence of any respondents is strong, they can handle it. If they think they are being targeted and can defend themselves, that is up to them.)

“At tayo naman po ay naniniwala, ang Pangulo ay naniniwala sa due process, naniniwala sa mga bawat ebidensiyang ilalahad at ipapakita, so doon na lang po ang Pangulo. Kung ano ang maibibigay na mga ebidensiya at dapat nating igalang,” Castro added.
(We believe—and the President believes—in due process and in the evidence that will be presented; so, the President’s position rests on that. We must respect whatever evidence is presented.)

In a statement on Monday, lawyer Ade Fajardo and Romualdez’s spokesperson said the Office of the Ombudsman appears to be trying to keep its case against Romualdez alive by issuing statements after witnesses recanted their testimonies.
Fajardo questioned its tag for Romualdez as a mastermind while the preliminary investigation is still ongoing.
He said such a label could create the impression that a conclusion has been reached even before its evaluation of evidence is completed and ahead of receiving Romualdez’s defense. /gsg

articles.title: Solon: Style, witness factors in Tolosa’s demeanor at impeachment trial
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Personal styles and the status of the witness presented were factors in why counsel for the prosecution Benjamin Tolosa Jr. appeared to be aggressive during the 21st day of Vice…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Personal styles and the status of the witness presented were factors in why counsel for the prosecution Benjamin Tolosa Jr. appeared to be aggressive during the 21st day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, lawmakers said on Wednesday.

During a press briefing while the Senate Impeachment Court was on a break, public prosecutor Manila Rep. Joel Chua and prosecution spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong were asked whether Tolosa’s manner of examining former Education Undersecretary Michael Poa was counterproductive, as netizens saw more of the rising tensions rather than the testimony being offered.
In response, Chua said that there are different styles and strategies for every lawyer, and Tolosa’s demeanor may have been due to his persona as a trial lawyer.

“‘Yong abugado naman kasi may kanya-kanyang style eh. So of course, as a lawyer, I cannot impose my style na mag-adopt siya sa style ko, ‘di ba, kasi kanya-kanya ‘yan eh, and we have to be mindful also na si Atty. Tolosa is a trial lawyer. So for the past several years, ‘yan talaga ‘yon kanyang forte,” Chua said.

(Lawyers have their own styles. So of course, as a lawyer, I cannot impose my style, ask him to adopt my style, because that varies from one individual to another, and we have to be mindful also that Atty. Tolosa is a trial lawyer. So for the past several years, that has been his forte.)
According to Chua, lawyers, especially those who are young, tend to be aggressive and eventually mellow down as they grow older.

“But insofar as the styles, ako tingin ko naman iba-iba naman ang mga styles, mas que sa mga defense makikita mo may mga gano’n din naman sa kanila, ‘di ba? So kung makikita mo talagang ‘yong mga trial lawyer talaga, lalo na ‘yong mga batang trial lawyer, they tend to be more aggressive,” he said.

(But insofar as the styles, I think there are different styles, even on the defense side you can see some of them doing that, right? So if you can see trial lawyers, especially the younger trial lawyers, they tend to be more aggressive.)
“Nagme-mellow (down) ka lang kapag medyo may edad ka na, so ‘wag mo nang tatanungin kung ilang taon na ako,” he jokingly added.
(They only mellow (down) if you are older, so do not ask how old I am.)

Alonto Adiong, meanwhile, said that the public should also understand that Tolosa was faced with a unique situation since he was examining Poa — a lawyer, an official close to the Vice President, and a member of the defense counsel.

“I think we also need to be conscious about the hostile witness in itself, because the hostile witness being presented is Atty. Michael Poa, he is not an ordinary hostile witness, he is one of the defense lawyers of the respondent,” he said.

“So legally speaking, he knows how the presentation will run. He is fully aware of that. So if you have observed, a portion of the discussions were on legal arguments premised on the rules of court, et cetera. This is expected because Atty. Poa, again, he’s not your ordinary hostile witness,” he added.
‘Laymanizing impeachment’

Chua refused to comment as to what he would have done differently if he was the one tasked to do the direct examination of Poa. However, Chua said that he tried his best — when he was examining two officials of the Land Bank of the Philippines from which Duterte’s offices withdrew their confidential funds (CFs) — to bring the discussions closer to the public by using layman’s terms.

According to the lawmaker, it might be hard for the private prosecutors to express in layman’s terms their queries since they have been accustomed to court proceedings — which are always formal and done in English.

“Iba-iba ‘yong style, nakita naman ninyo ako no’ng nag-present ako ng dalawang bank (officials), ginawa ko doon, mas ni-laymanize ko ‘di ba? So kasi in fairness din naman doon sa mga kasama nating mga abogado ngayon, they are trying their best to laymanize it, but siyempre sa tagal din naman ng kanilang practice, ‘yon na ‘yong kanilang nakagawian,” Chua said.

(There are different styles, you saw when I presented two bank (officials), what I did was to laymanize the discussions, right? So in fairness to our lawyers now, they are trying their best to laymanize it, but of course with the time they have been practicing law, they have been accustomed to trial setups.)

“At sa court hearing wala naman kasing nagta-Tagalog, lahat sa court hearing puro English. So we have to give them also credit na pinipilit nila na ipaliwanag ito sa wikang Tagalog, sa ating wika, kaya lang siyempre may mga bagay talaga na nakasanayan mo na o nakagawian mo na bilang isang trial lawyer,” he added.

(And in court hearings you would not hear people speaking Tagalog, the court hearing is done in English. So we have to give them credit that they are trying their best to deliver in Tagalog, in our language, but of course there are habits that you have become accustomed to as a trial lawyer.)

When asked if they would advise Tolosa to tone it down for the future, Alonto Adiong said that he would not do that since the lawyer was able to bring attention to the trial, and was very courteous despite his manner of asking Poa.

“First of all we cannot deny it, I think for this morning we were entertained, all of us, and that’s a fact, it only proved one thing — Atty. Jay Tolosa was really good at what he is doing. I think, for me, I did not want to blink, I think it kept you on the edge of your seat,” he said.

“I would not advise him to tone down, personally. Because the point is that he can actually send the message across, and both the defense and the presiding officer understood what he was talking about, and the witness understood what he was talking about. And I do not want him to tone down because he’s very, very respectful in the way that he laid down his (questions),” he added.

Sparks were flying between the lawyers early into Wednesday’s trial, as the atmosphere became tense after lead counsel for the respondent Sheila Sison questioned Tolosa’s offer where he called Poa “abugadong walang alam” (lawyer who knows nothing), claiming that it is mere “rhetoric aimed to provide drama.”

Tolosa said that it was not his intention to insult Poa, noting that he was merely referring to former Department of Education (DepEd) official’s insistence during a House of Representatives hearing in 2024 that he does not have personal knowledge of the confidential expenditures made by the agency in 2023.

Still, Sison asked that the statements be stricken out of record, as Tolosa could have used a better set of words. Escudero agreed with Sison, ruling that these words from Tolosa be removed from the records.

Eventually, the Senate Impeachment Court scolded Tolosa for engaging in “intramurals” with the defense lawyer and wasting time, as he started his examination of Poa by asking if the defense is willing to stipulate if he is a competent lawyer.

Poa is the tenth witness presented by the prosecution for Article I of the Articles of Impeachment, which delves on allegations of CF misuse within Duterte’s offices — DepEd and the Office of the Vice President (OVP).

Prior to Poa, the prosecution panel presented two Land Bank of the Philippines officials from which the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and DepEd withdrew their CFs; state auditors who checked on the confidential expenditures made by Duterte’s offices; OVP staffers like former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta; and on Tuesday, two Philippine Army (PA) officials. /mr

articles.title: AFP to MILF: Coordinate travel after convoy barred in Lanao Norte
articles.summary: LINAMON, Lanao del Norte – A military official reminded the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) to coordinate its movement with the Bangsamoro peace process mechanisms to avoid a repeat of…

blocks.text: LINAMON, Lanao del Norte – A military official reminded the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) to coordinate its movement with the Bangsamoro peace process mechanisms to avoid a repeat of Wednesday’s incident, which caused fear and panic among residents in Kolambugan, Lanao del Norte.

Some 200 MILF members, about half of whom were armed, were flagged down at a checkpoint by elements of the 52nd Mechanized Company under the 5th Mechanized Infantry “Kaagapay” Battalion and the 1st Provincial Mobile Force Company under the Lanao del Norte Provincial Police Office.
Government forces did not allow them to proceed to their destination in Camp Bilal, Munai, Lanao del Norte, where they would attend a meeting, due to a lack of coordination.
Brig. Gen. Bernardo Taqueban, commander of the 2nd Mechanized Infantry ” Magbalantay” Brigade, noted that the incident should dissuade other members of the MILF from doing the same again.
He stressed that law enforcers are imposing stricter security measures for the historic parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) on Sept. 14.
Taqueban said government forces notified the MILF convoy that they could not proceed, citing the lack of coordination and prohibition for MILF members to bring firearms.
“The MILF members under Lungga Dimaampao acknowledged the prohibition and went back to their point of origin and will no longer attend the meeting, ” Taqueban said.

Col. Leo Sua, Lanao del Norte provincial police director, said that police and military personnel conducted a checkpoint operation in Barangay Libertad, Kolambugan, at about 7:30 a.m. after receiving reports of a MILF convoy involving 23 vehicles and five motorcycles.

During the verification and inspection, the convoy of the MILF 131st Brigade failed to present pertinent documents or proof of prior coordination with the concerned authorities regarding its movement in the area, he said in a statement.

Lt. Col. Felimon Tan Jr., commanding officer of the 5th Mechanized “Kaagapay ” Battalion, and Sua facilitated the peaceful and orderly return of the MILF members at the boundary of Sultan Naga Dimaporo, Lanao del Norte, and Picong, Lanao del Sur, where the convoy originated./coa

articles.title: Koronadal air quality hits ‘very unhealthy’ level amid haze watch
articles.summary: KORONADAL CITY, South Cotabato — Air quality here worsened at certain hours since Tuesday, with fine particle pollution reaching “emergency” and “very unhealthy” levels as the Environmental…

blocks.text: KORONADAL CITY, South Cotabato — Air quality here worsened at certain hours since Tuesday, with fine particle pollution reaching “emergency” and “very unhealthy” levels as the Environmental Management Bureau-Region 12 (EMB-12) continued its haze watch.
Based on EMB’s special air quality monitoring, the PM2.5 Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 312.8 at 6 p.m. Tuesday, placing it under the “emergency” category.
Elevated levels were recorded at different times on Tuesday, including AQI readings of 213.8 at 4 p.m., 238.6 at 5 p.m., 213 at 7 p.m., and 203.9 at 10 p.m., all classified as “very unhealthy.”
Air quality improved after midnight, with readings returning to the “fair” category during the early hours of Wednesday, Sept. 2.
However, the AQI climbed again to 268.3 at 7 a.m. Wednesday, putting air quality back under the “very unhealthy” category. It dropped to 96, or “fair,” by 8 a.m.
The EMB said air quality can change depending on the time and environmental conditions and advised residents to keep checking official updates.

Rolly Doane Aquino, South Cotabato Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) chief, urged residents to take precautions, particularly those with respiratory and lung conditions.

“We should prepare our masks, especially for residents with respiratory and lung problems, and those with asthma and allergies. They should avoid too much exposure outdoors and use masks,” Aquino said.
He said the PDRRMO would coordinate with the Integrated Provincial Health Office (IPHO) for appropriate health advice and other measures.
The EMB-12 continues to closely monitor air quality in Koronadal under its haze watch and provide updates to the public.
The agency, however, did not say whether the elevated PM2.5 levels recorded in Koronadal were directly caused by haze coming from Indonesia./coa

articles.title: No eggs, no potatoes but ‘a lot of imagination’: how Spain cooked in war’s hunger years
articles.summary:
Book recreates recipes from period following end of Spanish civil war when people faced food shortages

Few dishes are simpler to prepare than Spain’s signature dish of tortilla de…

blocks.text: Few dishes are simpler to prepare than Spain’s signature dish of tortilla de patatas, which – aside from disputes about onions – requires nothing more than two basic ingredients and a pinch of salt. But where to begin if you have neither eggs nor potatoes?

That is the question the chef and food writer Berta Álvarez Acal sets out to answer in Recetas de Guerra (Wartime Recipes), a compilation of recipes covering the years of hunger after the end of the Spanish civil war in 1939.
In the case of the tortilla de patatas, the absent eggs and potatoes were substituted by moistened bread and onion to try to simulate the texture of an omelette.

“There was a formula using water, bicarbonate of soda and a bit of oil which simulated an egg perfectly and the potatoes are substituted by bread to make a tortilla that really is delicious,” Álvarez said.

blocks.caption: ‘Fried calamari without the calamari’. Álvarez says the recipes were recreated and shared with friends and family. Photograph: Berta Álvarez Acal

blocks.text: In the recipe for “fried squid without squid”, deep-fried onion rings masquerade as squid while the “wartime hake” is instead salt cod.
As for the “wartime and postwar breakfast”, this consists of “coffee” made from a blend of barley, malt and chicory.

“I got the idea for the book when I came across one of my great-aunt’s handwritten recipe books and I noticed that some of the recipes were marked ‘wartime’,” Álvarez said. “That led me to research recipes from other sources such as Ignacio Doménech, who wrote a book during the war about how to substitute ingredients and how to make the most of leftovers.”
She added: “Doménech showed us hundreds of examples of how, with a lot of imagination, we could survive those terrible days of starvation.”
Some of Doménech’s recipes, although born of privation, could well find themselves on the menu of an upmarket restaurant today, such as his rose petals with milk and honey.

Álvarez did not just compile the recipes. “We recreated them and shared them with friends and family,” she said. “Some dishes, although they were prepared from scraps, surprised us as they were real gems, others were not so great.”

The recipes in the book span the period from the founding of the second republic in 1931 to the phasing out of ration cards in 1952. In between, starvation stalked the land, especially in areas that supported the losing republican side in the civil war.
According to Miguel Ángel del Arco Blanco, a historian at the University of Granada, between 1939 and 1942 about 200,000 people died of starvation in Spain.
While people in the countryside could to some extent subsist on olives and whatever they could grow, Álvarez said “the hunger in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia was horrific”.
“It may seem implausible,” she said. “But for far too long, food in the postwar period was far worse than during the war.”

blocks.caption: Children queuing for milk rations in Barcelona in 1937.  Photograph: Daily Herald Archive/SSPL/Getty Images

blocks.text: Produce previously fed to livestock such as beetroot and turnips found its way to the table while the shortage of protein meant pets, cats in particular, were at risk.
“They were dangerous years for cats,” Álvarez said. “People used to put notices up in the hallway saying ‘please respect your neighbour’s cat’. But the cats lived on rats and were not good to eat.”

Álvarez said that what she learned while researching the book was to make the most of every kind of produce, adding that the book was also a homage to the generation that lived through those grim years. “I think it’s important that everyone knows what our grandparents lived through because it marked them as a generation. They were incredibly strong.”

articles.title: Historic Lunenburg, N.S., women's clothing store that's seen everything from bloomers to bikinis is closing
articles.summary: A longtime women's clothing store called Rudolf's Ladies Wear is closing its door after more than 100 years of operation, with Jane Lordly, the current manager and owner, having worked it for 40…

image.caption: Clearance signs at Rudolf's Ladies Wear. Jane Lordly says some of the signs she's using now were used by her grandfather when he ran the store decades ago. (Colin North/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

A longtime women's clothing store called Rudolf's Ladies Wear is closing its door after more than 100 years of operation, with Jane Lordly, the current manager and owner, having worked it for 40 years. Lordly says she received an offer for the space she couldn't refuse.
The store has been a constant presence in downtown Lunenburg since the early 1900s
A Lunenburg institution that has served the community for more than 100 years is coming to an end.
Rudolf’s Ladies Wear, a women’s clothing store on Lincoln Street, is closing this month.

Jane Lordly has been the owner and manager of Rudolf’s since taking over the shop 40 years ago. She says she had planned to continue running the store but received an offer for the space that she couldn’t ignore.
She's also struggled to find help.
"It's hard in Lunenburg because there's so many service jobs," she says. "It's hard to find people to work in retail now."
Lordly's grandfather, C. Ray Lohnes, took over the store in 1908, when it was called J. Joseph Rudolph's. He changed the name to Rudolf's.
After her grandfather passed, her grandmother didn't want to sell, so a manager was hired to run operations for 25 years before Lordly took the reins.

Rudolf’s established itself as the provider of women’s clothing for the clientele of Lunenburg. Lordly says she's seen many changes in what the store offered over the years, from bloomers to bikinis. She remembers when it was primarily a dress store and sold white pantyhose for nurses.

The closing of the shop is bittersweet, but Lordly says she’s ready to stop working seven days a week. She also says it's increasingly difficult to compete with online shopping and larger retailers in Bridgewater and Halifax.
For Lordly, the importance of the store for Lunenburg's older women makes the closing especially poignant.
"They might come in and buy a dress to be buried in," she says. "They'd always have one special dress."
Rudolf’s is one of the last pillars of an older Lunenburg; along with other long-standing stores such as Stan's Dad & Lad Shop and Kinley’s Drugstore.
Together they represent a series of longtime, family-owned brick and mortar stores.
Jamie Myra, the mayor of Lunenburg and owner of Stan’s, says he has early memories of Rudolf’s Ladies Wear as the face of Lincoln Street.

"My grandmother used to take me up on the second floor and I'd sit there while she went in and and tried on probably 25 dresses and probably bought one," says Myra. "But I remember that plain as day."

Myra says he thinks it’s inevitable that other Lunenburg stores will follow Rudolf's fate, and that galleries and service stores will be the main businesses operating within Lunenburg as the tourism industry grows.
He said the community will mourn one of its last landmark stores.
"This is one of the last original businesses that I can remember from my childhood days," he says.

items: More stories from the South Shore

blocks.text: The shelves and racks in Rudolf's are becoming increasingly empty due to the clearance sale. Lordly is using the same clearance signs that her grandfather used when he owned the store nearly a century ago.
In just a couple weeks, she’ll close the doors for good, ending this chapter in Lunenburg’s business history.
"I'll miss it," says Lordly. "I was quite happy doing it. I did my best."

articles.title: Ryanair warns air fares in Europe will jump next year if oil price stays high
articles.summary: Budget carrier says airlines could go bust as it cuts passenger targets to reduce exposure to ‘unhedged winter oil’

blocks.text: Ryanair has warned that air fares in Europe will jump next year if the oil price remains high and that some airlines could go bust.

The Irish budget carrier has cut its passenger target for the year to 31 March, down from 216 million customers to 214 million, to help reduce its exposure to “unhedged winter oil” during the unprofitable off season, with jet fuel currently trading at $140 (£104) a barrel.
Ryanair expects passenger numbers between November and March to be broadly flat compared with the same period last year.

The company said: “If high oil prices continue through to summer 2027, Ryanair believes short-haul air fares in Europe will increase materially to reflect higher oil prices, as some less well-hedged competitors will struggle to maintain capacity or even survive this coming winter season.”

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, touched $97.04 a barrel on Wednesday, the highest since late July, after renewed clashes between the US and Iran fuelled concerns over supply. It later eased back to just below $95.
after newsletter promotion

Ryanair expects the cut to its winter schedule to reduce its winter losses by €70m (£60m) to €100m. But, because it has hedged 80% of its jet fuel at $67 a barrel, it expects to record another profitable year, albeit below last year’s record profit after tax.

The airline said it was on track to increase summer passenger numbers – between April and October – by more than 5% from 138 million to 145 million. Fares are drifting “modestly down” between August and September compared with last year, as flagged in July.
The rival budget airline Wizz Air reported on Wednesday that its passenger numbers had grown by 25.9% last month compared with a year earlier, driven by a jump in flight capacity.

Ryanair was forced to reassure travellers in July that its planes were safe after a passenger was saved from being sucked out of a window mid-flight. Ljubisa Karović was sucked out headfirst after an engine failure resulted in parts smashing an acrylic window during a flight from Thessaloniki in Greece to Memmingen near Munich in Germany.
His wife, Svetlana Grković, saved her 61-year-old husband by holding on to his legs and managed to pull him back in with the help of two other passengers.

articles.title: TRB directs NLEX to provide three-hour notice for flood-related closures
articles.summary: The Department of Transportation (DOTr), through the Toll Regulatory Board (TRB), has told the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) Corporation to implement a faster and more efficient warning system for…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 4:56pm

The Department of Transportation (DOTr), through the Toll Regulatory Board (TRB), has told the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) Corporation to implement a faster and more efficient warning system for motorists during heavy rains and flooding.
In a statement, Transportation Secretary Banoy Lopez said the timely advisories will help motorists along NLEX avoid flood-related traffic and identify alternative routes.
In a letter to NLEX Corporation President and General Manager Luis Reñon, the TRB said the board expects the firm to monitor the water level of the Pampanga River and Tulaoc River.

"Accordingly, as part of proactive measures moving forward, every time there is anticipated rainfall, TRB expects that NLEX Corporation will monitor the water level of the Pampanga River and Tulaoc River," the TRB letter said.

"Should the water level approach the critical threshold, you are hereby directed to provide timely advisories to the motorists three hours before the expected rainfall through Variable Message Signs (VMS), portable VMS, and other communication platforms, that the San Simon-Pulilan Segment of NLEX will be closed to traffic and provide the affected motorists with an appropriate rerouting," it added.

The TRB said the NLEX Corporation is directed to closely coordinate with the DOTr and TRB to ensure the timely implementation of appropriate flood mitigation measures and other necessary interventions, with the primary objective of ensuring the safety of the motoring public and minimizing traffic disruption.

"Further, NLEX Corporation is also directed to consider the reimbursement of toll fees for motorists with Class 1 vehicles who were compelled to make a U-turn along NLEX due to the flooding incidents in the affected area," the TRB said. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood
articles.summary: Hopes of finding more survivors among the thousands still missing in Nepal were fading, authorities said on Wednesday, a week after a glacier collapse in the Himalayas unleashed flash floods that…

image.caption: Ayusha Timalsina, wife of Suraj Timalsina, who was killed in the deadly floods and a mudslide, mourns during his cremation rituals using an effigy (not pictured) as his body remained missing, in Kathmandu, Nepal. (Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Hopes of finding more survivors among the thousands still missing in Nepal were fading, authorities said on Wednesday, a week after a glacier collapse in the Himalayas unleashed flash floods that devastated the mountainous nation.
Death toll rises past 1,100 with nearly 4,000 people missing
Rescuers save over 100 in Nepal, thousands still missing

At least 1,114 people have been killed and nearly 4,000 remain unaccounted for, with officials fearing many are buried under debris left by the floods that tore through towns and valleys near the Chinese border.
Across the border in Tibet, China's official toll has held steady since Sunday at 16 dead and 546 missing.
"The hope of finding survivors is decreasing," Phanindra Paudel, a senior official at the government’s National Emergency Operation Center (NEOC), said. "We pray and are hopeful. Hope is hope!"

items: More than 1,000 dead from catastrophic Nepal-China floods as rescuers search for survivors
Nepal flash flood death toll climbs to 579, with 32 Canadians, permanent residents among missing

blocks.text: Rescuers are trying to find survivors believed to be trapped inside the tunnels of several hydroelectric plants, whose powerhouses have spaces and rooms for people to stay, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.
Authorities said 279 people had been rescued from the ruins of hydropower projects but at least 639 more were still missing, some of whom are believed to be trapped in tunnels.
Specialized rescue teams from India, China and the United States were involved in the tunnel rescue attempts, authorities said.
Tunnels search continues

"The plan today is to get on a helicopter and go to the hydro tunnels where they believe there's still life," Ferrin Cole, a member of the U.S. crisis response team that is currently in Nepal, told ANI news agency.
"We have high-technology listening equipment to listen for sounds of life. And then the safety teams to go in and check."

"Looking at the nature of the disaster and the area which has been hit by the flood, as days go by there are less chances of human survivors," Binoj Basnet, a retired senior army general who oversaw the search and rescue operation during the 2015 earthquake in which about 9,000 people were killed, said.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the focus would shift from search, rescue and relief operations towards rehabilitation and reconstruction.

"The government is now focusing on rehabilitation while working to protect the lives of people in the affected areas and providing necessary medical treatment and psychological counseling," Shah said in a late-night post on social media on Tuesday.

The disaster left at least 2.2 million tons of debris, according to a preliminary estimate by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), including parts of buildings, rocks, and sediment, the equivalent of six Empire State buildings.
Residents in affected areas walked around the remains of what were once bustling villages and towns, trying to salvage whatever they could of their belongings.
"My husband and I were able to escape safely. But we could not pick up anything," Shanta Sunar, 45, a small shopkeeper and survivor from Nuwakot, said.
"We have lost whatever we had. But we are lucky nothing happened to us."
Growing public health risk

United Nations spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said aid agencies were concerned about the growing public health risk from overcrowded shelters, contaminated water and damaged health facilities, particularly for women and children during the monsoon season.

About 3,900 people remain unaccounted for and nearly 3,500 people are living in 27 displacement sites across the hardest-hit districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa, Dujarric told a regular UN press briefing on Tuesday.
Shah said his government had stepped up surveillance and response measures to prevent possible outbreaks of disease in flood-affected areas.

articles.title: Poa: I didn't ask if rewards to informants from confidential funds resulted in success
articles.summary: Former DepEd undersecretary Michael Poa said that he did not ask the DepEd's disbursing officer if the payment of rewards to informants using confidential funds resulted in success.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 4:50pm

Former Department of Education undersecretary Michael Poa on Wednesday said that he did not ask the DepEd's special disbursing officer (SDO) if the payment of rewards to informants using P15 million of the department's confidential funds resulted in success in information-gathering.

Poa made the testimony during Day 21 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, at which he is also a member of the defense team. He was an official at DepEd when Duterte headed the department.

“Hindi po,” Poa responded when asked by Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian if he asked DepEd SDO Eduard Fajarda if it was Fajarda who disbursed the P15 million from the confidential funds as payment for rewards, and if that payment resulted in success in information gathering.
(No, I did not ask.)
“Hindi [ko] po [tinanong], kasi ang sinasabi parati po niya sa field, itatanong niya sa field. I understand field operatives,” Poa added.
(I did not ask because he always tell me that it was based on field, he will ask from the field.)
Gatchalian then noted that it was Fajarda’s mandate to disburse the confidential fund as the SDO and asked Poa again why he did not ask Fajarda on how the confidential fund was being disbursed.

“Hindi ko rin po tinanong na kung siya mismo ang nagbibigay kasi every time tatanungin ko siya kung saan makukuha ‘yung mga sagot sa AOM, ang parating [sagot] ay based sa field or tinatanong sa field,” Poa replied.
(I did not ask him further details because every time I ask him for answers to AOM, he tells me that the information is based on field inputs or asked from the field.)

An AOM is a written notification to the agency head and concerned officer/s informing of the deficiencies noted in the audit of accounts, operations or transactions and requiring comments thereto and/or submission of documentary and other information and requirements within a reasonable period.

The Commission on Audit issued an AOM on the P15-million DepEd fund spending, and it was Poa who answered the AOM even as he insisted that he had no personal knowledge on how the confidential fund of the DepEd was used. — BM, GMA News

Residents of Barangay Sta. Fe have been living on opposite sides of a river since Aug. 9, when the swollen river swept away the bridge that connects them to the town proper.

The bridge collapse cut off the northern portion of Sta. Fe from the rest of the community, leaving 800 residents dependent on improvised mechanisms for crossing and difficult alternate routes for food, medicine, and other necessities.

blocks.caption: Marocs visits isolated village in Zambales

articles.title: Cargo ship with 10 crew sinks off Istanbul – maritime authorities
articles.summary: ISTANBUL — A cargo ship sank in the Marmara Sea near Istanbul after colliding with a second vessel, with rescuers hunting 10 people who were on board, Turkish officials said Wednesday. The…

blocks.text: ISTANBUL — A cargo ship sank in the Marmara Sea near Istanbul after colliding with a second vessel, with rescuers hunting 10 people who were on board, Turkish officials said Wednesday.

The incident occurred before dawn when the ALSU, an empty oil tanker, collided with the Tugberk Imamoglu, a cargo ship carrying rolled steel, which sank shortly after, the transport ministry’s maritime directorate said on X.
The collision occurred 18 nautical miles off Silivri district on the western edge of Istanbul province, the governor’s office said on X.
“Due to the Tugberk İmamoglu not responding to any calls and the crew not answering their mobile phones… it is believed the dry cargo ship has sunk,” the maritime directorate said.
The ALSU’s captain had reported the collision as happening at 3:15 am (0015 GMT), with 14 search and rescue vessels dispatched to the area backed by a helicopter, it said.
“Life-saving equipment, including a lifeboat belonging to the Tugberk Imamoglu which had 10 crew members on board, has been found at sea. Unfortunately, the crew members were not inside.”
The ALSU, which was damaged in the collision, was also joining in search and rescue efforts, it said.
At the time of the collision, the Tugberk Imamoglu was carrying 4,200 tons of rolled sheet metal, it said.
The maritime directorate initially said the ALSU was carrying 3,000 tonnes of motor oil, but later said the tanker was empty in a detail confirmed by the governorate.
The incident took place three days after deadly ferry accident off Northern Cyprus in which eight Turkish nationals died with rescuers still hunting for another 20 people listed as missing. /dl

articles.title: `Very unhealthy’ air quality logged in parts of Zamboanga Peninsula
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – The Environmental Management Bureau-Region 9 (EMB-9) recorded poor air quality in parts of the Zamboanga Peninsula on Tuesday due to the haze from forest and…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – The Environmental Management Bureau-Region 9 (EMB-9) recorded poor air quality in parts of the Zamboanga Peninsula on Tuesday due to the haze from forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.

As of 12:00 p.m., the Particulate Matter Station-Western Mindanao State University San Ramon Campus in Barangay Talisayan, Zamboanga City recorded a “very unhealthy” PM2.5 level with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 159.

In contrast, the Differential Optical Absorption Spectroscopy- Ateneo de Zamboanga University Junior High School station in Barangay Tumaga, Zamboanga City registered good air quality, with PM2.5 at 48.

The EMB-9 warned that exposure to elevated PM2.5 levels poses health risks to the general population, particularly sensitive groups such as children, the elderly, and those with respiratory conditions.
Residents in affected areas were advised to limit outdoor activity, especially strenuous exercise; wear N95 masks when going outdoors; and keep doors and windows closed to reduce indoor exposure.
The EMB-9 urged the public to monitor official advisories and follow instructions from authorities.
It emphasized that air quality can fluctuate throughout the day and may differ across locations.
Communities were urged to share updates with schools, workplaces, and households to ensure public safety.
“Stay informed. Stay alert. Protect your health,” the bureau reminded./coa

articles.title: Sadiq Khan fined by fast-track court over untaxed car City Hall says is not his
articles.summary: London mayor convicted under controversial system where magistrates can decide outcomes in seconds

blocks.text: The London mayor, Sadiq Khan, has been convicted and fined for not taxing a 24-year-old car, through a controversial fast-track court system.

He was found guilty last month under a system critics have described as “conveyor-belt justice”, with magistrates deciding on hundreds of daily cases and sometimes spending less than a minute on them.
City Hall officials say the car does not belong to either Khan or Transport for London (TfL), raising the possibility he was wrongly convicted.

The mayor has been the focus of protests by motorists angry at the expansion of the ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) to cover the whole of London, who said they planned to register cars in Khan’s name – supposedly to make him liable for the £12.50 daily charge.

The prosecution was taken by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA), the government organisation that maintains databases of drivers, which accused Khan of being the keeper of the vehicle when it was spotted as being untaxed on 24 January.

A magistrate, sitting in a private hearing of the single justice procedure in Herefordshire, convicted Khan in his absence and ordered that he pay a £220 fine, £85 in costs and settle the £35.84 bill for unpaid tax on the Micra.
After the Press Association flagged the criminal conviction to the DVLA on Tuesday, officials confirmed they were reviewing the case and investigating the circumstances of the prosecution.

In a development that raised more questions, court documents show that DVLA letters addressed to the mayor about the unpaid tax bill were sent to a Gordon Ramsay restaurant in east London instead of the nearby TfL offices.
The mayor faces the possibility of having to appear in court in person to try to overturn the conviction.
after newsletter promotion

The single justice procedure was brought in in 2015 as a cheaper method of dealing with low-level criminal cases, allowing magistrates to sit alone and in private to hand out convictions rather than sitting in open court.

The system, which is under government review, was criticised in 2024 when about 59,000 train-fare evasion convictions had to be overturned for being unlawful and it emerged children had been wrongly convicted in the secretive courts.
It has also been the focus of intensifying scrutiny thanks to regular incidents of sick and incapacitated pensioners being harshly convicted for not paying their household bills.

In Khan’s case, court records seen by the Press Association show he was prosecuted by the DVLA after the annual tax on the blue Nissan Micra, which was first registered in 2002, ran out in September last year.
The DVLA has been approached for comment.
